# User stories

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Format

- Stories: `US-nnn`, "As a … I want … so that …", plus in-scope and out-of-scope notes.
- Acceptance criteria are given in `acceptance-criteria.md` as `AC-nnn-nn` (Given/When/Then), one observable behaviour each, each citing its `US` and any `BR`; the agent does not derive them.
- Do not invent behaviour a story does not state; record the gap as an `OQ` in `scope.md`.

## Stories

Epic: as a conference organizer, I want participants to register online, so that registrations are collected and managed reliably.

### US-001 External participant registration

As an external participant, I want to register using the external participant form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities I select.
In scope: the external form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: payment, accounts, editing a submitted registration.

### US-002 Student registration

As a student, I want to register using the student form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities available to students.
In scope: the student form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: verifying student status externally, accounts.

### US-003 Configurable conference options

As an organizer, I want workshops, events, meals and other optional activities to be configurable, so that the system can be reused when the programme changes.
Out of scope: an administration UI for options.

### US-004 Registration confirmation

As a participant, I want a clear confirmation in the application after my registration is processed, so that I know it was received (BR-06).

### US-005 Reliable registration storage

As an organizer, I want every accepted registration stored reliably, so that none is lost and each can be recovered (BR-07).

### US-006 Participant email confirmation

As a participant, I want an email confirming my registration, so that I have a record of it.

### US-007 Organizer notification

As an organizer, I want an email when someone registers, containing the submitted data with the raw registration JSON attached, so that I can monitor incoming registrations.

### US-008 Registration export

As an organizer, I want to export the current registrations as an Excel workbook, so that I can process them outside the system (BR-08).

### US-009 Organizer registration search

As an organizer, I want to search and filter the registrations in the application, so that I can find a participant or a group of participants without exporting every registration (BR-09, BR-10).
In scope: an organizer page and API that list registrations with a text search and filters by registration type and selected option, paged. Out of scope: editing or deleting registrations from the list, exporting the filtered list, saved searches.
 Kept until the operator deletes them; no automatic deletion. The release notes tell the operator to delete the database rows and JSON copies no later than 12 months after the conference. |Allowed; each registration is stored separately and the export shows both. |No limit per category; each option at most once per registration, duplicates are rejected. |The registration stays accepted (HTTP 201, confirmation shown). Emails are sent only after the database row and the JSON copy exist; an email failure is logged with the registration id only, no personal data. |Consents are part of the conference configuration (id, wording, mandatory). The shipped configuration has one mandatory consent `privacy`: "I agree that my personal data is processed for organizing the conference and that it is shared with the conference organizers." |Every option carries a configured list of registration types it is available to (default: both); the backend rejects an option that is not available to the registration type. |# Scope

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## In scope

- Registration forms for external participants and students (US-001, US-002)
- Configurable conference options (US-003)
- In-application confirmation, participant confirmation email, organizer notification email with the JSON attachment (US-004, US-006, US-007)
- Storage in the database plus a raw JSON copy (US-005)
- Excel export for organizers (US-008)
- Anti-automation protection of the registration form
- Organizer search and filter page for registrations (US-009)

## Out of scope

- Participant accounts and login
- Payment processing
- Editing or cancelling a submitted registration
- Verifying student status externally
- An administration UI or dashboard, including option configuration; the organizer search page of US-009 is the only organizer page
- Integration with an identity provider

## Priorities

1. A registration is never lost: storage (BR-07) comes before any notification.
2. Security and privacy (`project/02_design/security-requirements.md`) come before convenience.
3. The participant flow (US-001 to US-006) comes before organizer features (US-007, US-008).

## Open questions

| ID | Question | Owner | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| OQ-01 | Are all options available to students, or are some only for external participants? | Product owner | Every option carries a configured list of registration types it is available to (default: both); the backend rejects an option that is not available to the registration type. |
| OQ-02 | Which mandatory consents exist, and what is their wording? | Product owner | Consents are part of the conference configuration (id, wording, mandatory). The shipped configuration has one mandatory consent `privacy`: "I agree that my personal data is processed for organizing the conference and that it is shared with the conference organizers." |
| OQ-03 | What happens when storage succeeds but an email fails? | Product owner | The registration stays accepted (HTTP 201, confirmation shown). Emails are sent only after the database row and the JSON copy exist; an email failure is logged with the registration id only, no personal data. |
| OQ-04 | How many options may a participant select per category? | Product owner | No limit per category; each option at most once per registration, duplicates are rejected. |
| OQ-05 | Is a second registration with the same email allowed? | Product owner | Allowed; each registration is stored separately and the export shows both. |
| OQ-06 | How long are registrations and JSON copies kept? | Product owner | Kept until the operator deletes them; no automatic deletion. The release notes tell the operator to delete the database rows and JSON copies no later than 12 months after the conference. |

The answers are the product owner's decisions and hold for every run of this project; the agent records no decision for them. A new question that arises later becomes a decision record as usual.
# Business rules

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Rules

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| BR-01 | There are two registration types: external participant and student. Each has the fixed fields listed under Data; configuration never changes them. |
| BR-02 | Required fields are never empty; leading and trailing whitespace is not significant. |
| BR-03 | Email has a valid email format. Text accepts Unicode, including Slovenian characters (č, š, ž). |
| BR-04 | Options are grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities. Only active options can be selected; unknown or inactive options are rejected. |
| BR-05 | Mandatory consents must be given and are never preselected. |
| BR-06 | The in-application confirmation is shown only after the registration was accepted. |
| BR-07 | An accepted registration is stored in the database and as a raw JSON copy on persistent storage. |
| BR-08 | Only organizers can obtain the registration list; it is not reachable without organizer access. |
| BR-09 | Only organizers can search and list registrations; the same organizer access as the export (BR-08) applies. |
| BR-10 | The search text matches, without regard to upper or lower case, any part of the first name, last name, email, organization or study institution; leading and trailing whitespace is ignored and an empty text matches every registration. Filters combine: a registration is listed only if it matches the text, the type filter and the option filter. Results are listed newest first, 20 per page, with the total number of matches. |

## Data

| Form or entity | Fields (all required) |
|---|---|
| External participant | first name, last name, email, organization / institution |
| Student | first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID |
| Conference option | stable identifier, display name, category (workshop, event, meal, other), active or inactive |
| Consent | which consents exist and their wording: `OQ-02` |

## Glossary

- Participant: a person who registers, external or student.
- Organizer: conference staff who receive notifications and export registrations.
- Option: a selectable workshop, event, meal or other activity.
- Active option: an option currently offered for selection.
- Raw JSON copy: the registration exactly as accepted, stored as a file for backup.
# Requirements check

# Acceptance criteria

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 3, 6 · Agent: read-only

This list is an input, the same in every run of this project: the agent does not derive, add, merge or reword criteria. Each criterion states one observable behaviour (Given / When / Then) and cites its story and rules. "Rejected" always means: the API answers with an error status and field errors, no database row and no JSON copy are created, and no email is sent. The open questions are answered in `scope.md` (OQ-01 to OQ-06).

Common terms used below:

- *valid external submission*: registration type `EXTERNAL`; first name, last name, email, organization filled; every mandatory consent given; a reCAPTCHA token the verifier accepts; zero or more distinct active option ids available to the type.
- *valid student submission*: as above with type `STUDENT` and study institution, study programme and student ID instead of organization.

## US-001 External participant registration

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-001-01 | Given active options are configured, when a valid external submission is sent, then it is accepted (HTTP 201) and the response contains the new registration id. | BR-01, BR-04 |
| AC-001-02 | Given the external form, when any one required field (first name, last name, email, organization) is missing, empty or only whitespace, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that field. | BR-01, BR-02 |
| AC-001-03 | Given a valid external submission whose text fields have leading and trailing spaces, when it is accepted, then the stored values have the spaces removed. | BR-02 |
| AC-001-04 | Given the external form, when the email does not have a valid email format, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the email field. | BR-03 |
| AC-001-05 | Given the external form, when an option id is unknown, inactive or listed twice, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the options. | BR-04, SR-04, OQ-04 |
| AC-001-06 | Given the external form, when a mandatory consent is not given, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that consent. | BR-05, OQ-02 |
| AC-001-07 | Given the external form, when the reCAPTCHA token is missing or the verifier rejects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) and nothing is stored. | SR-01, scope (anti-automation) |
| AC-001-08 | Given the registration page, when the participant chooses "external participant", then the page shows exactly the external fields, the active options grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities, and every consent checkbox unchecked. | BR-01, BR-04, BR-05 |

## US-002 Student registration

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-002-01 | Given active options are configured, when a valid student submission is sent, then it is accepted (HTTP 201) and the response contains the new registration id. | BR-01, BR-04 |
| AC-002-02 | Given the student form, when any one required field (first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID) is missing, empty or only whitespace, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that field. | BR-01, BR-02 |
| AC-002-03 | Given the student form, when the email does not have a valid email format, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the email field. | BR-03 |
| AC-002-04 | Given an active option configured as not available to students, when a student submission selects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the options. | BR-04, OQ-01 |
| AC-002-05 | Given the student form, when a mandatory consent is not given, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that consent. | BR-05, OQ-02 |
| AC-002-06 | Given the student form, when the reCAPTCHA token is missing or the verifier rejects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) and nothing is stored. | SR-01 |
| AC-002-07 | Given the registration page, when the participant chooses "student", then the page shows exactly the student fields and only the active options available to students, grouped by category, with every consent checkbox unchecked. | BR-01, BR-04, BR-05, OQ-01 |

## US-003 Configurable conference options

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-003-01 | Given a configuration with active and inactive options, when the form configuration is requested, then it lists only the active options, each with its identifier, display name, category and the registration types it is available to. | BR-04 |
| AC-003-02 | Given the backend is started with a different options configuration (an option added, one deactivated), when the form configuration is requested, then it reflects the new configuration, with no code change. | AR-04 |
| AC-003-03 | Given an options configuration that is invalid (duplicate identifier, unknown category, missing name), when the backend starts, then it refuses to start. | AR-04 |

## US-004 Registration confirmation

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-004-01 | Given a filled form, when the backend accepts the registration, then the page shows a confirmation with the participant's name and the selected options, and the form is no longer shown. | BR-06 |
| AC-004-02 | Given a filled form, when the backend rejects the registration with field errors, then no confirmation is shown, each error is shown next to its field, and the entered values remain. | BR-06, NFR-03 |
| AC-004-03 | Given a form with an empty required field or an invalid email, when the participant submits, then the page shows the field errors and sends no request to the backend. | NFR-03 |
| AC-004-04 | Given a filled form, when the backend fails or cannot be reached, then no confirmation is shown and a general error message without technical details is shown. | BR-06, SB-07 |

## US-005 Reliable registration storage

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-005-01 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then the database holds one registration with the type, every submitted field, the selected options, each consent with the time it was given, and the time of registration. | BR-07 |
| AC-005-02 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then a JSON copy named after the registration id exists in the JSON copy directory and contains the registration as accepted. | BR-07 |
| AC-005-03 | Given the JSON copy cannot be written, when a valid submission is sent, then the API answers with an error (not 201) and no registration is left in the database. | BR-07, AR-05 |
| AC-005-04 | Given a valid submission with Slovenian characters (č, š, ž, Č, Š, Ž) in the names and institution, when it is accepted, then the database row and the JSON copy contain the text unchanged. | BR-03, NFR-01 |

## US-006 Participant email confirmation

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-006-01 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then one email is sent to the participant's address naming the conference, the participant and the selected options. | US-006 |
| AC-006-02 | Given a submission whose text fields contain line breaks, header-like text or HTML markup, when the confirmation email is sent, then the email has no additional headers or recipients and the markup appears only as literal text. | SR-05 |
| AC-006-03 | Given the mail server is unavailable, when a valid submission is sent, then the registration is still accepted (HTTP 201) and stored. | OQ-03, OQ-03 |

## US-007 Organizer notification

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-007-01 | Given organizer addresses are configured, when a registration is accepted, then each organizer address receives a notification email containing the submitted registration data. | US-007 |
| AC-007-02 | Given a registration is accepted, when the organizer notification is sent, then it has a JSON attachment whose content equals the stored JSON copy. | US-007, BR-07, SR-07 |

## US-008 Registration export

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-008-01 | Given stored registrations, when an organizer requests the export with valid organizer credentials, then the response is an Excel workbook (`.xlsx`) with one row per registration, containing its type, fields, selected options, consents and registration time. | BR-08 |
| AC-008-02 | Given stored registrations, when the export is requested without credentials or with wrong credentials, then it is refused (HTTP 401) and no registration data is returned. | BR-08, SB-02 |
| AC-008-03 | Given a registration with Slovenian characters, when the organizer exports, then the workbook cell contains the text unchanged. | NFR-01 |
| AC-008-04 | Given organizer HTTPS-only access is on, when the export is requested with valid credentials over plain HTTP from a client that is not on localhost, then it is refused and no registration data is returned. | SR-06 |

## US-009 Organizer registration search

*Search request*: an organizer request to list registrations with an optional text, an optional registration type (`EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT`), an optional option id and an optional page number (default 1).

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-009-01 | Given stored registrations, when an organizer sends a search request with valid credentials and no text or filters, then the response lists the registrations newest first, at most 20, each with its id, type, first name, last name, email, organization or study institution, selected option ids and registration time, together with the total number of registrations. | BR-09, BR-10 |
| AC-009-02 | Given stored registrations, when the search text is part of a registration's first name, last name, email, organization or study institution in any upper or lower case, then that registration is listed and registrations without such a match are not. | BR-10 |
| AC-009-03 | Given stored external and student registrations, when the type filter is `STUDENT`, then only student registrations are listed. | BR-10 |
| AC-009-04 | Given stored registrations, when the option filter names an option id, then only registrations that selected that option are listed. | BR-10 |
| AC-009-05 | Given stored registrations, when a text, a type filter and an option filter are given together, then only registrations matching all three are listed. | BR-10 |
| AC-009-06 | Given stored registrations, when no registration matches, then the response is successful with an empty list and a total of 0. | BR-10 |
| AC-009-07 | Given 25 matching registrations, when page 1 and page 2 are requested, then page 1 lists the newest 20 and page 2 the remaining 5, and both report a total of 25. | BR-10 |
| AC-009-08 | Given the search request, when the type is unknown, the option id is not a configured option, the page number is below 1 or the text is longer than 100 characters, then the request is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that parameter. | BR-10, SB-01 |
| AC-009-09 | Given stored registrations, when the search is requested without credentials or with wrong credentials, then it is refused (HTTP 401) and no registration data is returned. | BR-09, SB-02 |
| AC-009-10 | Given organizer HTTPS-only access is on, when the search is requested with valid credentials over plain HTTP from a client that is not on localhost, then it is refused and no registration data is returned. | SR-06 |
| AC-009-11 | Given a registration with Slovenian characters (č, š, ž, Č, Š, Ž) in the last name, when an organizer searches for that last name, then the registration is listed and the text is unchanged. | BR-03, NFR-01 |
| AC-009-12 | Given the organizer page, when the organizer enters valid credentials, then the page shows the registration list with a search field, a type filter, an option filter and page navigation; with wrong credentials it shows an error and no registration data. | BR-09, BR-10 |
| AC-009-13 | Given a registration whose text fields contain HTML markup or script, when it is shown on the organizer page, then the markup appears only as literal text and is not executed. | SR-09 |

## Traceability

| Story | Criteria |
|---|---|
| US-001 | AC-001-01 … AC-001-08 |
| US-002 | AC-002-01 … AC-002-07 |
| US-003 | AC-003-01 … AC-003-03 |
| US-004 | AC-004-01 … AC-004-04 |
| US-005 | AC-005-01 … AC-005-04 |
| US-006 | AC-006-01 … AC-006-03 |
| US-007 | AC-007-01, AC-007-02 |
| US-008 | AC-008-01 … AC-008-04 |
| US-009 | AC-009-01 … AC-009-13 |

Total: 48 criteria.

Requirements without their own criterion, covered in the specification and verified in phase 6: SR-03 rate and size limits, NFR-02 persistence across container recreation, NFR-04 health and readiness (runtime demonstration).
=====
# End-to-end scenarios

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 3, 6 · Agent: read-only

The end-to-end tests of this project: exactly one test per scenario below, run against the real local stack (`docker compose up`: frontend, backend, PostgreSQL, Mailpit) through the browser, and the same in every run of this project. The agent writes no other end-to-end test and no scenario is merged or split. Each scenario names the criteria it demonstrates; the acceptance tests (one or more per criterion) carry the detailed cases, so an end-to-end test checks the journey once and does not repeat them.

| ID | Scenario | Steps and observations | Covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| E2E-01 | External participant registers | Open the page, choose "external participant", fill the form with valid data, select at least one option per category, submit. The page shows the confirmation. The database holds the registration, the JSON copy exists, the participant email and the organizer email (with the JSON attachment) are in Mailpit. | AC-001-01, AC-001-08, AC-004-01, AC-005-01, AC-005-02, AC-006-01, AC-007-01, AC-007-02, DoD-P01 to DoD-P03 |
| E2E-02 | Student registers | As E2E-01 with "student": only the student fields and student-available options are shown; the registration is stored and both emails arrive. | AC-002-01, AC-002-07, AC-004-01, DoD-P01 to DoD-P03 |
| E2E-03 | Field errors are shown next to the fields | Submit the form with an empty required field and an invalid email: errors appear next to the fields and no request reaches the backend; then make the backend reject a submission (for example an unavailable option): the backend's field errors appear next to their fields and the entered values remain. | AC-004-02, AC-004-03, NFR-03 |
| E2E-04 | Slovenian characters survive the whole chain | Register with č, š, ž, Č, Š, Ž in the names and institution. The text is unchanged in the page confirmation, the database row, the JSON copy, both emails and the exported workbook. | AC-005-04, AC-008-03, NFR-01 |
| E2E-05 | Organizer exports registrations | Request the export with valid organizer credentials: a valid Excel workbook with one row per registration is downloaded. The same request without credentials is refused (HTTP 401) and returns no data. | AC-008-01, AC-008-02, DoD-P04 |
| E2E-06 | Organizer searches registrations | Register one external and one student participant with known, distinct last names and options. Open the organizer page, enter wrong credentials: an error is shown and no data. Enter valid credentials: both registrations are listed. Search for the student's last name: only the student is listed. Clear the text and filter by type "external": only the external participant is listed. | AC-009-01, AC-009-02, AC-009-03, AC-009-12, DoD-P06 |

Not end-to-end tests (verified by runtime demonstration in phase 6): NFR-02 (data survives recreation of every container) and NFR-04 (health and readiness).

# API contract

> Owner: Architect · Read in: phases 2, 3, 4, 6 · Agent: read-only

The REST API between the frontend or organizer and the backend is fixed by this file (AR-09): paths, methods, field names, status codes and the local test settings below are the same in every run of this project, so that external checks can use them. Everything not stated here (internal design, additional optional response fields, the OpenAPI document written in phase 2) is the agent's choice. The phase 2 contract in `docs/02_contracts/` must describe exactly this API.

## Local stack

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Backend base URL | `http://127.0.0.1:8080` (published by `02_output/docker-compose.yml`) |
| Mailpit web and API | `http://127.0.0.1:8025` |
| reCAPTCHA test mode | setting `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`; then the token `test-pass` is accepted and every other token is rejected |

| REST API (`/api`) | `02_contracts/openapi.json` (exactly `api-contract.md`) |

## 2. REST API

Exactly as `api-contract.md` (AR-09); the agent's choices where it is silent:

| Topic | Choice |
|---|---|
| Registration id | UUID (string) |
| `GET /api/form-config` extra field | `captchaTestMode` (boolean), so the frontend knows to send `test-pass` instead of rendering the widget |
| Error body for 401, 403, 413, 415, 429, 500 | same shape `{"errors":[{"field":…,"message":…}]}` with `field` `credentials`, `protocol`, `body`, `request` or `server`; never registration data or internals |
| Malformed JSON or wrong field type | 400 with `field` `body` |
| Unknown `type` in a registration | 400 with `field` `type` |
| Search page beyond the last page | 200, `items` empty, `total` and `page` as requested |
| Search `option` | any configured option id, active or inactive (G-01 in `01_requirements-check.md`, G-04); unknown id → 400 `option` |
| Search `type` | exactly `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT` (case-sensitive), else 400 `type` |
| Search `page` | integer ≥ 1, else (including non-numbers) 400 `page` |
| Search `text` | trimmed; more than 100 characters (before trimming) → 400 `text` |
| Export row order | registration time ascending, then id |
| Organizer over plain HTTP from a non-local client | 403, `field` `protocol` (D-11) |

## 3. Backend architecture (AR-02, AR-03)

Ports and adapters under `si.konferenca.registration`:

| Package | Contains | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | registration model, types, option catalogue, validation rules, search criteria; plain Java | nothing else in the project (no Spring, no Jakarta Persistence) |
| `application` | use cases (`RegisterParticipant`, `SearchRegistrations`, `ExportRegistrations`, `FormConfiguration`) and the ports they need (`RegistrationStore`, `JsonCopyStore`, `CaptchaVerifier`, `Notifier`, `WorkbookWriter`) | `domain` |
| `adapter.persistence` | JPA entities, Spring Data repositories, `RegistrationStore` implementation | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.jsoncopy` | file `JsonCopyStore` | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.mail` | `Notifier` over Spring Mail | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.captcha` | Google verify client and test-mode verifier | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.export` | Apache POI `WorkbookWriter` | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.web` | controllers, request and response DTOs, error mapping, servlet filters (rate limit, body size, HTTPS-only) | `application`, `domain` |
| `config` | Spring wiring, settings, startup checks, security configuration, options loading | everything |

Justification: the rules (validation, catalogue, search criteria) are the part most worth mutation testing and are kept free of frameworks; each external system sits behind one port, so it can be replaced by a test double in acceptance tests (mail failure, JSON copy failure, captcha). Adapters do not depend on each other. The ArchUnit rules check exactly this table plus no package cycles (slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` and `adapter.(*)..`).

## 4. Business behaviour

### 4.1 Conference configuration (US-003, AR-04, BR-04, OQ-01, OQ-02)

- One JSON file (schema `conference-config.schema.json`) holds the options and consents. Its location is the setting `CONFERENCE_CONFIG` (Spring resource: `classpath:conference.json` or `file:/path`); the shipped `classpath:conference.json` holds the programme and the consent `privacy` with the wording of OQ-02.
- Loaded once at startup. Start-up fails (the application refuses to start) when: the file is missing or not valid JSON; an option or consent id is duplicate, empty or not `[a-z0-9-]{1,64}`; a category is not one of `WORKSHOP`, `EVENT`, `MEAL`, `OTHER`; a name or consent text is missing or blank; `availableTo` contains an unknown type or is empty; `active` or `mandatory` is not a boolean. A missing `availableTo` means both types (OQ-01).
- `GET /api/form-config` lists only active options in file order, with `id`, `name`, `category`, `availableTo`; all consents; `captchaSiteKey` and `captchaTestMode`.
- Changing the programme means editing the file (or pointing `CONFERENCE_CONFIG` at another file) and restarting; the fixed participant fields never come from it (BR-01).

### 4.2 Registration (US-001, US-002, SB-01)

Validation on the backend, all errors of one request collected (one entry per field):

| Rule | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| V-01 | Every text field is trimmed (leading and trailing Unicode whitespace) before validation and storage (AC-001-03). |
| V-02 | Required fields per type (BR-01): both types `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`; `EXTERNAL` `organization`; `STUDENT` `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`. Missing, empty or blank → error for the field. Fields of the other type are ignored and stored as null. Maximum lengths: names 100, `organization` and `studyInstitution` 200, `studyProgramme` 200, `studentId` 50; longer → error. |
| V-03 | `email`: at most 254 characters, one `@`, a non-empty local part and a domain with a dot, no whitespace or control characters; otherwise error `email`. |
| V-04 | `type` missing or not `EXTERNAL`/`STUDENT` → error `type` (then only the common fields are checked). |
| V-05 | `options`: at most 50 entries; each must be an active configured option available to the type; a duplicate id → error `options` (SR-04, OQ-04). |
| V-06 | `consents`: every mandatory consent must be listed; unknown ids → error `consents` (BR-05). |
| V-07 | `captchaToken` missing or blank → error `captchaToken`; otherwise the verifier is asked (6.3) and a rejection is error `captchaToken`. The verifier is asked even when other fields fail, so one response reports everything. |

Text accepts any Unicode letters (BR-03); control characters other than none are rejected in single-line fields. A valid request is stored (5.2), then emails are sent (6), then 201 `{"id"}` is returned.

### 4.3 Search (US-009, BR-09, BR-10)

- Parameters validated as in section 2. Matching: `text` (trimmed, lower-cased) is a substring of lower-cased `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization` or `studyInstitution`; `LIKE` wildcards in the text are escaped; empty text matches all. `type` and `option` filters are combined with AND.
- Order `registeredAt` descending, then `id` descending; page size 20; response `total`, `page`, `items` with the fields of `api-contract.md` (`options` as ids).
- Parameterised queries only (SB-05).

### 4.4 Export (US-008, BR-08, SR-07)

- `GET /api/export` returns an `.xlsx` (`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`), first sheet `registrations`, header row and columns exactly as `api-contract.md`; every value is a string cell (never a formula), `registeredAt` as ISO 8601 UTC text, cells of the other type empty.
- Only the listed registration fields; no internal columns.

## 5. Storage

### 5.1 Database (AR-06, ES-08, SB-05)

Tables `registration`, `registration_option`, `registration_consent` created by Flyway `V1__registration.sql` (contract `database.md`); JPA with `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`. Each consent is stored with the time it was given (= registration time); `registered_at` is the server's time in UTC.

### 5.2 One unit of work (AR-05, BR-07, OQ-03)

1. Validate (4.2).
2. In one database transaction: insert the registration rows; write the JSON copy to `<JSON_COPY_DIR>/<id>.json.tmp`, flush and sync, atomically rename to `<id>.json`.
3. If writing the copy fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 (AC-005-03). If the commit fails after the copy was written, the copy is deleted.
4. Only after the commit are the emails sent (6). A mail failure is logged with the registration id only and does not change the 201 (AC-006-03).

### 5.3 JSON copy and Unicode (NFR-01)

The copy (schema `registration-copy.schema.json`) is the registration as accepted: `id`, `type`, the eight participant fields (null where not applicable), `options`, `consents` (`id`, `givenAt`), `registeredAt`. UTF-8 without escaping non-ASCII letters, so č, š, ž appear unchanged; the database uses UTF-8; emails use UTF-8; the workbook stores Unicode strings.

### 5.4 Personal data (SB-12 … SB-14)

Only the fields of BR-01 plus options, consents and their time are collected; purposes and retention as in `security-requirements.md` and OQ-06 (no automatic deletion; release notes tell the operator to delete rows and copies within 12 months after the conference). Consent checkboxes are never preselected (7.1).

## 6. External services

### 6.1 Participant email (US-006, SR-05)

Plain text (`text/plain; charset=UTF-8`), contract `emails.md`. Subject from configuration only (`Registration confirmed: <CONFERENCE_NAME>`); recipient the validated email; body names the conference, the participant and the selected options by display name. No user input goes into a header; markup is literal text in a plain text body. SMTP connect, read and write timeouts 5 s.

### 6.2 Organizer notification (US-007, SR-07)

One message to every address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`, plain text listing the registration's fields, with the attachment `registration-<id>.json` (`application/json`) whose bytes are the stored JSON copy.

### 6.3 reCAPTCHA (SR-01, SR-02, AR-07)

- Production path: `POST` form `secret`, `response` to `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` (default `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify`); accepted only when the JSON answer has `"success": true`; timeouts, errors and other answers reject. Tested against a mocked endpoint (DoD-P05).
- Test mode (`CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`): only the token `test-pass` is accepted; no network call.
- The site key comes from `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` through `GET /api/form-config`; the secret key never leaves the backend.

## 7. Frontend

Single page app, routes by path: `/` registration, `/organizer` organizer page; nginx falls back to `index.html`. Only `/api` is called (AR-01), same origin through the nginx proxy. Contract `ui.md`.

### 7.1 Registration page (AC-001-08, AC-002-07, AC-004-01, NFR-03)

- Loads `GET /api/form-config`; a choice "External participant" / "Student"; after the choice it shows exactly that type's fields, the active options available to the type in four groups (Workshops, Events, Meals, Other activities; empty groups hidden), every consent unchecked, and the captcha (widget or test-mode notice).
- Client validation mirrors V-01 … V-03 and mandatory consents; on error it shows each message next to its field and sends nothing (AC-004-03).
- On 201 it replaces the form with a confirmation showing the participant's name and the selected options' names (AC-004-01).

### 7.2 Organizer page (AC-009-12, AC-009-13, SR-09)

- A login form (username, password); credentials are kept in memory only and sent as HTTP Basic with `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest` (so no browser login dialog appears).
- On success: search field, type filter (all / external / student), option filter (all configured options from the form configuration plus "all"), a result table, total count and previous/next page navigation. 401 → "Wrong username or password." and no data.
- All data is rendered as React text nodes (never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`), so markup is literal (SR-09).

### 7.3 Errors (AC-004-02, AC-004-04, SB-07)

400 field errors are shown next to their fields and the entered values stay; any other failure or network error shows "Your registration could not be sent. Please try again later." without technical details.

## 8. Security

### 8.1 Organizer access (SB-02, SB-03, PA-04)

Spring Security HTTP Basic on `GET /api/export` and `GET /api/registrations`, one in-memory user from `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` and `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`; the password is hashed with BCrypt at start-up and only the hash is kept. Everything else under `/api` is public; `/actuator/health/**` is public; all other paths are denied. Stateless, no session, CSRF off (no cookies are used).

### 8.2 HTTPS-only organizer access (SR-06, AC-008-04, AC-009-10)

With `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=true` (default), a request to an organizer endpoint is answered 403 before credentials are checked unless it is secure or local:

One error handler maps exceptions to the error body of section 2; 500 says only "Internal error". Logs name registration ids, never names, emails or other personal data, tokens or credentials.

### 8.6 Health (ES-09, NFR-04)

Actuator `health` only, with liveness and readiness groups; readiness includes the database and a check that the JSON copy directory is writable; the mail health indicator is off (a mail outage must not make the service unready).

## 9. Configuration (ES-01, ES-02, SR-02)

| Setting | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `APP_ENVIRONMENT` | `production` | `local`, `test` or `production`; the unsafe settings below are refused in production |
| `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL`, `SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME` | none | compose and tests set them |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | none (secret) | |
| `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_TLS`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | none, `587`, `true`, empty, empty | compose: Mailpit, TLS off |
| `MAIL_FROM` | `registration@konferenca.si` | |
| `CONFERENCE_NAME` | `Conference` | |
| `CONFERENCE_CONFIG` | none | compose and tests: `classpath:conference.json`; required |
| `JSON_COPY_DIR` | `/data/json-copies` | named volume `json-copies` |
| `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | `false` | production refuses `true` |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | empty | production refuses empty |
| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | Google siteverify | overridden only in tests |
| `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`, `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | none (secrets) | required in every environment |
| `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | `true` | production refuses `false`; compose default `false` (local plain HTTP) |
| `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` | empty (no CORS) | production refuses a value |
| `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`, `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` | `60`, `16384` | |

Secrets have no default in code or in committed files; `.env` is git-ignored (ES-02).

## 10. Deployment (NFR-02, NFR-04, SB-04, SB-11, SR-08)

`02_output/docker-compose.yml`: `db` (postgres, volume `pgdata`, `pg_isready` health check), `mailpit` (ports `127.0.0.1:8025`, `127.0.0.1:1025`), `backend` (image from `backend/Dockerfile` with the jar built by `./mvnw package`, port `127.0.0.1:8080`, volume `json-copies`, readiness health check, user `app`), `frontend` (multi-stage `frontend/Dockerfile`, nginx as user `nginx` on port 8080 published as `127.0.0.1:8081`, proxies `/api` to `backend:8080` with `Host` set to the upstream and `X-Forwarded-For` set to `$remote_addr`, health check). Production: an external nginx terminates TLS (SB-04), sets `Host`, `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Forwarded-Proto` itself (SR-08); the backend README gives the required proxy settings.

## 11. Quality and scanning (SB-08, SB-09)

Format (Spotless, Prettier), lint (PMD, ESLint), type check (`tsc`), static analysis (SpotBugs, PMD, Semgrep), duplication (CPD, jscpd), dependency scan (Dependency-Check, `npm audit`), secret scan (Gitleaks); coverage JaCoCo and V8; mutation PIT and Stryker, scopes as in `quality-requirements.md`.

| Rule | Behaviour |
|---|---|

| V-02 | Required fields per type (BR-01): both types `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`; `EXTERNAL` `organization`; `STUDENT` `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`. | V-03 | `email`: at most 254 characters, one `@`, a non-empty local part and a domain with a dot, no whitespace or control characters; otherwise error `email`. |
| V-04 | `type` missing or not `EXTERNAL`/`STUDENT` → error `type` (then only the common fields are checked). |
| V-05 | `options`: at most 50 entries; each must be an active configured option available to the type; a duplicate id → error `options` (SR-04, OQ-04). |
| V-06 | `consents`: every mandatory consent must be listed; unknown ids → error `consents` (BR-05). |

## 1. Components and interfaces

|---|---|---|---|
| backend | `02_output/backend` | java, spring-boot-starter-* , flyway, postgresql, poi-ooxml | `eclipse-temurin` JRE image, user `app` |

|---|---|
| REST API (`/api`) | `02_contracts/openapi.json` (exactly `api-contract.md`) |
| JSON copy file | `02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json` |

Contracts are validated by `02_contracts/validate-contracts.mjs` (JSON parser, local `$ref` resolution, and a comparison of paths, methods, status codes and fields against `api-contract.md`).

## 2. REST API

Exactly as `api-contract.md` (AR-09); the agent's choices where it is silent:

| Topic | Choice |
|---|---|
| Registration id | UUID (string) |
| `GET /api/form-config` extra field | `captchaTestMode` (boolean), so the frontend knows to send `test-pass` instead of rendering the widget |
| Error body for 401, 403, 413, 415, 429, 500 | same shape `{"errors":[{"field":…,"message":…}]}` with `field` `credentials`, `protocol`, `body`, `request` or `server`; never registration data or internals |
| Malformed JSON or wrong field type | 400 with `field` `body` |
| Unknown `type` in a registration | 400 with `field` `type` |
| Search page beyond the last page | 200, `items` empty, `total` and `page` as requested |
| Search `option` | any configured option id, active or inactive (G-01 in `01_requirements-check.md`, G-04); unknown id → 400 `option` |
| Search `type` | exactly `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT` (case-sensitive), else 400 `type` |
| Search `page` | integer ≥ 1, else (including non-numbers) 400 `page` |
| Search `text` | trimmed; more than 100 characters (before trimming) → 400 `text` |
| Export row order | registration time ascending, then id |
| Organizer over plain HTTP from a non-local client | 403, `field` `protocol` (D-11) |

## 3. Backend architecture (AR-02, AR-03)

Ports and adapters under `si.konferenca.registration`:

| Package | Contains | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | registration model, types, option catalogue, validation rules, search criteria; plain Java | nothing else in the project (no Spring, no Jakarta Persistence) |
| `application` | use cases (`RegisterParticipant`, `SearchRegistrations`, `ExportRegistrations`, `FormConfiguration`) and the ports they need (`RegistrationStore`, `JsonCopyStore`, `CaptchaVerifier`, `Notifier`, `WorkbookWriter`) | `domain` |
| `adapter.persistence` | JPA entities, Spring Data repositories, `RegistrationStore` implementation | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.jsoncopy` | file `JsonCopyStore` | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.mail` | `Notifier` over Spring Mail | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.captcha` | Google verify client and test-mode verifier | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.export` | Apache POI `WorkbookWriter` | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.web` | controllers, request and response DTOs, error mapping, servlet filters (rate limit, body size, HTTPS-only) | `application`, `domain` |
| `config` | Spring wiring, settings, startup checks, security configuration, options loading | everything |

Justification: the rules (validation, catalogue, search criteria) are the part most worth mutation testing and are kept free of frameworks; each external system sits behind one port, so it can be replaced by a test double in acceptance tests (mail failure, JSON copy failure, captcha). Adapters do not depend on each other. The ArchUnit rules check exactly this table plus no package cycles (slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` and `adapter.(*)..`).

## 4. Business behaviour

### 4.1 Conference configuration (US-003, AR-04, BR-04, OQ-01, OQ-02)

- One JSON file (schema `conference-config.schema.json`) holds the options and consents. Its location is the setting `CONFERENCE_CONFIG` (Spring resource: `classpath:conference.json` or `file:/path`); the shipped `classpath:conference.json` holds the programme and the consent `privacy` with the wording of OQ-02.
- Loaded once at startup. Start-up fails (the application refuses to start) when: the file is missing or not valid JSON; an option or consent id is duplicate, empty or not `[a-z0-9-]{1,64}`; a category is not one of `WORKSHOP`, `EVENT`, `MEAL`, `OTHER`; a name or consent text is missing or blank; `availableTo` contains an unknown type or is empty; `active` or `mandatory` is not a boolean. A missing `availableTo` means both types (OQ-01).
- `GET /api/form-config` lists only active options in file order, with `id`, `name`, `category`, `availableTo`; all consents; `captchaSiteKey` and `captchaTestMode`.
- Changing the programme means editing the file (or pointing `CONFERENCE_CONFIG` at another file) and restarting; the fixed participant fields never come from it (BR-01).

### 4.2 Registration (US-001, US-002, SB-01)

Validation on the backend, all errors of one request collected (one entry per field):

| Rule | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| V-01 | Every text field is trimmed (leading and trailing Unicode whitespace) before validation and storage (AC-001-03). |
| V-02 | Required fields per type (BR-01): both types `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`; `EXTERNAL` `organization`; `STUDENT` `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`. Missing, empty or blank → error for the field. Fields of the other type are ignored and stored as null. Maximum lengths: names 100, `organization` and `studyInstitution` 200, `studyProgramme` 200, `studentId` 50; longer → error. |
| V-03 | `email`: at most 254 characters, one `@`, a non-empty local part and a domain with a dot, no whitespace or control characters; otherwise error `email`. |
| V-04 | `type` missing or not `EXTERNAL`/`STUDENT` → error `type` (then only the common fields are checked). |
| V-05 | `options`: at most 50 entries; each must be an active configured option available to the type; a duplicate id → error `options` (SR-04, OQ-04). |
| V-06 | `consents`: every mandatory consent must be listed; unknown ids → error `consents` (BR-05). |
| V-07 | `captchaToken` missing or blank → error `captchaToken`; otherwise the verifier is asked (6.3) and a rejection is error `captchaToken`. The verifier is asked even when other fields fail, so one response reports everything. |

Text accepts any Unicode letters (BR-03); control characters other than none are rejected in single-line fields. A valid request is stored (5.2), then emails are sent (6), then 201 `{"id"}` is returned.

### 4.3 Search (US-009, BR-09, BR-10)

- Parameters validated as in section 2. Matching: `text` (trimmed, lower-cased) is a substring of lower-cased `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization` or `studyInstitution`; `LIKE` wildcards in the text are escaped; empty text matches all. `type` and `option` filters are combined with AND.
- Order `registeredAt` descending, then `id` descending; page size 20; response `total`, `page`, `items` with the fields of `api-contract.md` (`options` as ids).
- Parameterised queries only (SB-05).

### 4.4 Export (US-008, BR-08, SR-07)

- `GET /api/export` returns an `.xlsx` (`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`), first sheet `registrations`, header row and columns exactly as `api-contract.md`; every value is a string cell (never a formula), `registeredAt` as ISO 8601 UTC text, cells of the other type empty.
- Only the listed registration fields; no internal columns.

## 5. Storage

### 5.1 Database (AR-06, ES-08, SB-05)

Tables `registration`, `registration_option`, `registration_consent` created by Flyway `V1__registration.sql` (contract `database.md`); JPA with `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`. Each consent is stored with the time it was given (= registration time); `registered_at` is the server's time in UTC.

### 5.2 One unit of work (AR-05, BR-07, OQ-03)

1. Validate (4.2).
2. In one database transaction: insert the registration rows; write the JSON copy to `<JSON_COPY_DIR>/<id>.json.tmp`, flush and sync, atomically rename to `<id>.json`.
3. If writing the copy fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 (AC-005-03). If the commit fails after the copy was written, the copy is deleted.
4. Only after the commit are the emails sent (6). A mail failure is logged with the registration id only and does not change the 201 (AC-006-03).

### 5.3 JSON copy and Unicode (NFR-01)

The copy (schema `registration-copy.schema.json`) is the registration as accepted: `id`, `type`, the eight participant fields (null where not applicable), `options`, `consents` (`id`, `givenAt`), `registeredAt`. UTF-8 without escaping non-ASCII letters, so č, š, ž appear unchanged; the database uses UTF-8; emails use UTF-8; the workbook stores Unicode strings.

### 5.4 Personal data (SB-12 … SB-14)

Only the fields of BR-01 plus options, consents and their time are collected; purposes and retention as in `security-requirements.md` and OQ-06 (no automatic deletion; release notes tell the operator to delete rows and copies within 12 months after the conference). Consent checkboxes are never preselected (7.1).

## 6. External services

### 6.1 Participant email (US-006, SR-05)

Plain text (`text/plain; charset=UTF-8`), contract `emails.md`. Subject from configuration only (`Registration confirmed: <CONFERENCE_NAME>`); recipient the validated email; body names the conference, the participant and the selected options by display name. No user input goes into a header; markup is literal text in a plain text body. SMTP connect, read and write timeouts 5 s.

### 6.2 Organizer notification (US-007, SR-07)

One message to every address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`, plain text listing the registration's fields, with the attachment `registration-<id>.json` (`application/json`) whose bytes are the stored JSON copy.

### 6.3 reCAPTCHA (SR-01, SR-02, AR-07)

- Production path: `POST` form `secret`, `response` to `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` (default `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify`); accepted only when the JSON answer has `"success": true`; timeouts, errors and other answers reject. Tested against a mocked endpoint (DoD-P05).
- Test mode (`CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`): only the token `test-pass` is accepted; no network call.
- The site key comes from `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` through `GET /api/form-config`; the secret key never leaves the backend.

## 7. Frontend

Single page app, routes by path: `/` registration, `/organizer` organizer page; nginx falls back to `index.html`. Only `/api` is called (AR-01), same origin through the nginx proxy. Contract `ui.md`.

### 7.1 Registration page (AC-001-08, AC-002-07, AC-004-01, NFR-03)

- Loads `GET /api/form-config`; a choice "External participant" / "Student"; after the choice it shows exactly that type's fields, the active options available to the type in four groups (Workshops, Events, Meals, Other activities; empty groups hidden), every consent unchecked, and the captcha (widget or test-mode notice).
- Client validation mirrors V-01 … V-03 and mandatory consents; on error it shows each message next to its field and sends nothing (AC-004-03).
- On 201 it replaces the form with a confirmation showing the participant's name and the selected options' names (AC-004-01).

### 7.2 Organizer page (AC-009-12, AC-009-13, SR-09)

- A login form (username, password); credentials are kept in memory only and sent as HTTP Basic with `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest` (so no browser login dialog appears).
- On success: search field, type filter (all / external / student), option filter (all configured options from the form configuration plus "all"), a result table, total count and previous/next page navigation. 401 → "Wrong username or password." and no data.
- All data is rendered as React text nodes (never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`), so markup is literal (SR-09).

### 7.3 Errors (AC-004-02, AC-004-04, SB-07)

400 field errors are shown next to their fields and the entered values stay; any other failure or network error shows "Your registration could not be sent. Please try again later." without technical details.

## 8. Security

### 8.1 Organizer access (SB-02, SB-03, PA-04)

Spring Security HTTP Basic on `GET /api/export` and `GET /api/registrations`, one in-memory user from `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` and `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`; the password is hashed with BCrypt at start-up and only the hash is kept. Everything else under `/api` is public; `/actuator/health/**` is public; all other paths are denied. Stateless, no session, CSRF off (no cookies are used).

### 8.2 HTTPS-only organizer access (SR-06, AC-008-04, AC-009-10)

With `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=true` (default), a request to an organizer endpoint is answered 403 before credentials are checked unless it is secure or local:
- secure: the connection is TLS, or the direct peer is a trusted proxy (loopback or private address) and sent `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`;
- local: the client address is loopback, where the client address is the direct peer, or, when the peer is a trusted proxy that sent `X-Forwarded-For`, the last address in it.
Production refuses to start with `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false`.

### 8.3 Rate and size limits (SR-03, SB-06)

- Fixed one-minute window per client address (as in 8.2) and endpoint (method and path) for every `/api` endpoint; over `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` (default 60) → 429. Failed organizer logins count against the same limit.
- Request bodies over `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` (default 16384) → 413, checked from `Content-Length` and while reading.

### 8.4 Errors and logs (SB-07, ES-07)

One error handler maps exceptions to the error body of section 2; 500 says only "Internal error". Logs name registration ids, never names, emails or other personal data, tokens or credentials.

### 8.5 Headers (SB-10)

Backend: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. Frontend nginx: CSP `default-src 'self'` allowing the reCAPTCHA script and frame origins (`https://www.google.com/recaptcha/`, `https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/`), `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`.

### 8.6 Health (ES-09, NFR-04)

Actuator `health` only, with liveness and readiness groups; readiness includes the database and a check that the JSON copy directory is writable; the mail health indicator is off (a mail outage must not make the service unready).

+| `adapter.web` | controllers, request and response DTOs, error mapping, servlet filters (rate limit, body size, HTTPS-only) | `application`, `domain` |
+| `config` | Spring wiring, settings, startup checks, security configuration, options loading | everything |

+Justification: the rules (validation, catalogue, search criteria) are the part most worth mutation testing and are kept free of frameworks; each external system sits behind one port, so it can be replaced by a test double in acceptance tests (mail failure, JSON copy failure, captcha). Adapters do not depend on each other. The ArchUnit rules check exactly this table plus no package cycles (slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` and `adapter.(*)..`).
+### 4.1 Conference configuration (US-003, AR-04, BR-04, OQ-01, OQ-02)

+- One JSON file (schema `conference-config.schema.json`) holds the options and consents. Its location is the setting `CONFERENCE_CONFIG` (Spring resource: `classpath:conference.json` or `file:/path`); the shipped `classpath:conference.json` holds the programme and the consent `privacy` with the wording of OQ-02.

+- Loaded once at startup. Start-up fails (the application refuses to start) when: the file is missing or not valid JSON; an option or consent id is duplicate, empty or not `[a-z0-9-]{1,64}`; a category is not one of `WORKSHOP`, `EVENT`, `MEAL`, `OTHER`; a name or consent text is missing or blank; `availableTo` contains an unknown type or is empty; `active` or `mandatory` is not a boolean. A missing `availableTo` means both types (OQ-01).
+- `GET /api/form-config` lists only active options in file order, with `id`, `name`, `category`, `availableTo`; all consents; `captchaSiteKey` and `captchaTestMode`.
+- Changing the programme means editing the file (or pointing `CONFERENCE_CONFIG` at another file) and restarting; the fixed participant fields never come from it (BR-01).
+Validation on the backend, all errors of one request collected (one entry per field):
+| V-01 | Every text field is trimmed (leading and trailing Unicode whitespace) before validation and storage (AC-001-03). |

+| V-02 | Required fields per type (BR-01): both types `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`; `EXTERNAL` `organization`; `STUDENT` `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`. Missing, empty or blank → error for the field. Fields of the other type are ignored and stored as null. Maximum lengths: names 100, `organization` and `studyInstitution` 200, `studyProgramme` 200, `studentId` 50; longer → error. |
+| V-03 | `email`: at most 254 characters, one `@`, a non-empty local part and a domain with a dot, no whitespace or control characters; otherwise error `email`. |
+| V-04 | `type` missing or not `EXTERNAL`/`STUDENT` → error `type` (then only the common fields are checked). |
+| V-05 | `options`: at most 50 entries; each must be an active configured option available to the type; a duplicate id → error `options` (SR-04, OQ-04). |
+| V-06 | `consents`: every mandatory consent must be listed; unknown ids → error `consents` (BR-05). |

+| V-07 | `captchaToken` missing or blank → error `captchaToken`; otherwise the verifier is asked (6.3) and a rejection is error `captchaToken`. The verifier is asked even when other fields fail, so one response reports everything. |

+Text accepts any Unicode letters (BR-03); control characters other than none are rejected in single-line fields. A valid request is stored (5.2), then emails are sent (6), then 201 `{"id"}` is returned.

+- Parameters validated as in section 2. Matching: `text` (trimmed, lower-cased) is a substring of lower-cased `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization` or `studyInstitution`; `LIKE` wildcards in the text are escaped; empty text matches all. `type` and `option` filters are combined with AND.
+- Order `registeredAt` descending, then `id` descending; page size 20; response `total`, `page`, `items` with the fields of `api-contract.md` (`options` as ids).

+- `GET /api/export` returns an `.xlsx` (`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`), first sheet `registrations`, header row and columns exactly as `api-contract.md`; every value is a string cell (never a formula), `registeredAt` as ISO 8601 UTC text, cells of the other type empty.
+- Only the listed registration fields; no internal columns.

+Tables `registration`, `registration_option`, `registration_consent` created by Flyway `V1__registration.sql` (contract `database.md`); JPA with `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`. Each consent is stored with the time it was given (= registration time); `registered_at` is the server's time in UTC.
+### 5.2 One unit of work (AR-05, BR-07, OQ-03)
+2. In one database transaction: insert the registration rows; write the JSON copy to `<JSON_COPY_DIR>/<id>.json.tmp`, flush and sync, atomically rename to `<id>.json`.
+3. If writing the copy fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 (AC-005-03). If the commit fails after the copy was written, the copy is deleted.
+4. Only after the commit are the emails sent (6). A mail failure is logged with the registration id only and does not change the 201 (AC-006-03).

+The copy (schema `registration-copy.schema.json`) is the registration as accepted: `id`, `type`, the eight participant fields (null where not applicable), `options`, `consents` (`id`, `givenAt`), `registeredAt`. UTF-8 without escaping non-ASCII letters, so č, š, ž appear unchanged; the database uses UTF-8; emails use UTF-8; the workbook stores Unicode strings.

+Only the fields of BR-01 plus options, consents and their time are collected; purposes and retention as in `security-requirements.md` and OQ-06 (no automatic deletion; release notes tell the operator to delete rows and copies within 12 months after the conference). Consent checkboxes are never preselected (7.1).

+Plain text (`text/plain; charset=UTF-8`), contract `emails.md`. Subject from configuration only (`Registration confirmed: <CONFERENCE_NAME>`); recipient the validated email; body names the conference, the participant and the selected options by display name. No user input goes into a header; markup is literal text in a plain text body. SMTP connect, read and write timeouts 5 s.

+One message to every address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`, plain text listing the registration's fields, with the attachment `registration-<id>.json` (`application/json`) whose bytes are the stored JSON copy.

+- Production path: `POST` form `secret`, `response` to `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` (default `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify`); accepted only when the JSON answer has `"success": true`; timeouts, errors and other answers reject. Tested against a mocked endpoint (DoD-P05).
+- Test mode (`CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`): only the token `test-pass` is accepted; no network call.
+- The site key comes from `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` through `GET /api/form-config`; the secret key never leaves the backend.

+Single page app, routes by path: `/` registration, `/organizer` organizer page; nginx falls back to `index.html`. Only `/api` is called (AR-01), same origin through the nginx proxy. Contract `ui.md`.

+- Loads `GET /api/form-config`; a choice "External participant" / "Student"; after the choice it shows exactly that type's fields, the active options available to the type in four groups (Workshops, Events, Meals, Other activities; empty groups hidden), every consent unchecked, and the captcha (widget or test-mode notice).
+- Client validation mirrors V-01 … V-03 and mandatory consents; on error it shows each message next to its field and sends nothing (AC-004-03).
+- On 201 it replaces the form with a confirmation showing the participant's name and the selected options' names (AC-004-01).
+- A login form (username, password); credentials are kept in memory only and sent as HTTP Basic with `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest` (so no browser login dialog appears).

+- On success: search field, type filter (all / external / student), option filter (all configured options from the form configuration plus "all"), a result table, total count and previous/next page navigation. 401 → "Wrong username or password." and no data.
+- All data is rendered as React text nodes (never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`), so markup is literal (SR-09).

+400 field errors are shown next to their fields and the entered values stay; any other failure or network error shows "Your registration could not be sent. Please try again later." without technical details.

+Spring Security HTTP Basic on `GET /api/export` and `GET /api/registrations`, one in-memory user from `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` and `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`; the password is hashed with BCrypt at start-up and only the hash is kept. Everything else under `/api` is public; `/actuator/health/**` is public; all other paths are denied. Stateless, no session, CSRF off (no cookies are used).
+With `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=true` (default), a request to an organizer endpoint is answered 403 before credentials are checked unless it is secure or local:
+- secure: the connection is TLS, or the direct peer is a trusted proxy (loopback or private address) and sent `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`;
+- local: the client address is loopback, where the client address is the direct peer, or, when the peer is a trusted proxy that sent `X-Forwarded-For`, the last address in it.

+- Fixed one-minute window per client address (as in 8.2) and endpoint (method and path) for every `/api` endpoint; over `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` (default 60) → 429. Failed organizer logins count against the same limit.
+- Request bodies over `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` (default 16384) → 413, checked from `Content-Length` and while reading.
+One error handler maps exceptions to the error body of section 2; 500 says only "Internal error". Logs name registration ids, never names, emails or other personal data, tokens or credentials.

+Backend: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. Frontend nginx: CSP `default-src 'self'` allowing the reCAPTCHA script and frame origins (`https://www.google.com/recaptcha/`, `https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/`), `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`.

+Actuator `health` only, with liveness and readiness groups; readiness includes the database and a check that the JSON copy directory is writable; the mail health indicator is off (a mail outage must not make the service unready).
+| `APP_ENVIRONMENT` | `production` | `local`, `test` or `production`; the unsafe settings below are refused in production |
+| `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL`, `SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME` | none | compose and tests set them |
+| `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_TLS`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | none, `587`, `true`, empty, empty | compose: Mailpit, TLS off |
+| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | Google siteverify | overridden only in tests |
+| `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | `true` | production refuses `false`; compose default `false` (local plain HTTP) |
+| `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` | empty (no CORS) | production refuses a value |
+Secrets have no default in code or in committed files; `.env` is git-ignored (ES-02).

+`02_output/docker-compose.yml`: `db` (postgres, volume `pgdata`, `pg_isready` health check), `mailpit` (ports `127.0.0.1:8025`, `127.0.0.1:1025`), `backend` (image from `backend/Dockerfile` with the jar built by `./mvnw package`, port `127.0.0.1:8080`, volume `json-copies`, readiness health check, user `app`), `frontend` (multi-stage `frontend/Dockerfile`, nginx as user `nginx` on port 8080 published as `127.0.0.1:8081`, proxies `/api` to `backend:8080` with `Host` set to the upstream and `X-Forwarded-For` set to `$remote_addr`, health check). Secrets come from `.env` via `--env-file`; `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE`, `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` and `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` are passed from the environment. Production: an external nginx terminates TLS (SB-04), sets `Host`, `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Forwarded-Proto` itself (SR-08); the backend README gives the required proxy settings.

+Format (Spotless, Prettier), lint (PMD, ESLint), type check (`tsc`), static analysis (SpotBugs, PMD, Semgrep), duplication (CPD, jscpd), dependency scan (Dependency-Check, `npm audit`), secret scan (Gitleaks); coverage JaCoCo and V8; mutation PIT and Stryker, scopes as in `quality-requirements.md`.

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `docs/02_specification.md` 6.1, 6.2, SR-05, SR-07 · Agent: writes

Sent over SMTP (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_TLS`, optional `SMTP_USERNAME`/`SMTP_PASSWORD`) from `MAIL_FROM`, only after the registration and its JSON copy are committed (AR-05). Connect, read and write timeouts 5 s. A failure is logged as `Email for registration <id> failed` and never changes the API answer (OQ-03).

## Participant confirmation (US-006)

| Part | Value |
|---|---|
| To | the registration's `email` (validated: no whitespace or control characters) |
| Subject | `Registration confirmed: <CONFERENCE_NAME>` (configuration only, no user input) |
| Body | `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`; lines: greeting with first and last name, `Your registration for <CONFERENCE_NAME> was received.`, `Registration id: <id>`, `Selected options:` followed by one `- <option name>` per option (or `- none`) |

## Organizer notification (US-007)

| Part | Value |
|---|---|
| To | every address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` (comma separated, trimmed) |
| Subject | `New registration: <CONFERENCE_NAME>` |
| Body | `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`; `<label>: <value>` lines for id, type, first name, last name, email, the type's institution fields, options (ids), consents (ids), registered at |
| Attachment | `registration-<id>.json`, `application/json`, the exact bytes of the stored JSON copy (AC-007-02) |

User input appears only in plain text bodies, so line breaks, header-like text and markup stay literal text (AC-006-02); no header is built from user input except the participant address, which V-03 restricts.

# reCAPTCHA contract

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `docs/02_specification.md` 6.3, SR-01, SR-02, AR-07 · Agent: writes

## Widget (frontend)

When `GET /api/form-config` returns `captchaTestMode: false`, the frontend loads `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api.js?render=explicit`, renders a reCAPTCHA v2 checkbox with `captchaSiteKey` and sends `grecaptcha.getResponse()` as `captchaToken`; after a rejected submission the widget is reset. With `captchaTestMode: true` it shows "reCAPTCHA test mode" and sends `test-pass`. The site key is the frontend's only key (AR-07).

## Verify call (backend)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | `POST <RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL>`, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, fields `secret=<RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY>`, `response=<captchaToken>` |
| Default URL | `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify` |
| Accepted | HTTP 200 and JSON body with `"success": true` |
| Rejected | `"success": false`, any other status, unparsable body, timeout (5 s connect, 5 s read) or connection error |
| Test mode | `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`: no call; `test-pass` accepted, every other token rejected |
| Production guard | `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production` refuses to start with test mode on, or with an empty site or secret key (SR-02) |

The production path is tested against a mocked verification endpoint returning success and failure (DoD-P05).

| Option groups | one group (`fieldset` with legend) per non-empty category in this order: `Workshops`, `Events`, `Meals`, `Other activities`; one checkbox per active option available to the chosen type, labelled with the option name, unchecked |
| Consents | one checkbox per consent labelled with its text, unchecked; mandatory ones marked "(required)" |
| Captcha | reCAPTCHA widget, or the text `reCAPTCHA test mode` |
| Submit | button `Register` |
| Field error | text next to its field, linked by `aria-describedby`, `role="alert"` not used per field; options error next to the option groups, consent error next to the consents, captcha error next to the captcha |
| General error | `role="alert"`: `Your registration could not be sent. Please try again later.` |
| Confirmation | heading `Registration received`, text `Thank you, <first name> <last name>.`, a list of the selected options' names (or `No options selected`); the form is removed |

Client-side messages: `This field is required.`, `Enter a valid email address.`, `This consent is required.`. Backend messages are shown as returned.

## Organizer page `/organizer`

| Element | Accessible name / text |
|---|---|
| Login | text box `Username`, password box `Password`, button `Sign in` |
| Login error | `role="alert"`: `Wrong username or password.`; no registration data shown |
| Search | search box `Search`, select `Type` (`All types`, `External participant`, `Student`), select `Option` (`All options` plus every configured option name), button `Search` |
| Result | text `<total> registrations`, a table with columns `Registered`, `Type`, `First name`, `Last name`, `Email`, `Organization / institution`, `Options`; one row per item |
| Paging | buttons `Previous`, `Next` (disabled at the ends), text `Page <n> of <m>` |
| Empty result | `No registrations found.` |

Every value is rendered as text, never as HTML (SR-09).

# Database contract

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `docs/02_specification.md` 5.1, AR-06 · Agent: writes

PostgreSQL, UTF-8. Created only by Flyway migrations in `backend/src/main/resources/db/migration` (AR-06); the first is `V1__registration.sql`. JPA validates against it (`ddl-auto=validate`).

| Table | Column | Type | Null | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `registration` | `id` | `uuid` | no | primary key |
| | `type` | `varchar(16)` | no | `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT` (check constraint) |
| | `first_name` | `varchar(100)` | no | trimmed |
| | `last_name` | `varchar(100)` | no | trimmed |
| | `email` | `varchar(254)` | no | trimmed |
| | `organization` | `varchar(200)` | yes | `EXTERNAL` only |
| | `study_institution` | `varchar(200)` | yes | `STUDENT` only |
| | `study_programme` | `varchar(200)` | yes | `STUDENT` only |
| | `student_id` | `varchar(50)` | yes | `STUDENT` only |
| | `registered_at` | `timestamptz` | no | index `registration_registered_at_idx (registered_at desc, id desc)` |
| `registration_option` | `registration_id` | `uuid` | no | FK `registration(id)` on delete cascade |
| | `option_id` | `varchar(64)` | no | primary key (`registration_id`, `option_id`); index on `option_id` |
| `registration_consent` | `registration_id` | `uuid` | no | FK `registration(id)` on delete cascade |
| | `consent_id` | `varchar(64)` | no | primary key (`registration_id`, `consent_id`) |
| | `given_at` | `timestamptz` | no | |

Option and consent ids are the configuration's identifiers (`conference-config.schema.json`); they are not foreign keys, so a stored registration survives a configuration change. All queries are parameterised (SB-05).

# Email contract

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `docs/02_specification.md` 6.1, 6.2, SR-05, SR-07 · Agent: writes

Sent over SMTP (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_TLS`, optional `SMTP_USERNAME`/`SMTP_PASSWORD`) from `MAIL_FROM`, only after the registration and its JSON copy are committed (AR-05). Connect, read and write timeouts 5 s. A failure is logged as `Email for registration <id> failed` and never changes the API answer (OQ-03).

## Participant confirmation (US-006)

| Part | Value |
|---|---|
| To | the registration's `email` (validated: no whitespace or control characters) |
| Subject | `Registration confirmed: <CONFERENCE_NAME>` (configuration only, no user input) |
| Body | `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`; lines: greeting with first and last name, `Your registration for <CONFERENCE_NAME> was received.`, `Registration id: <id>`, `Selected options:` followed by one `- <option name>` per option (or `- none`) |

## Organizer notification (US-007)

| Part | Value |
|---|---|
| To | every address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` (comma separated, trimmed) |
| Subject | `New registration: <CONFERENCE_NAME>` |
| Body | `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`; `<label>: <value>` lines for id, type, first name, last name, email, the type's institution fields, options (ids), consents (ids), registered at |
| Attachment | `registration-<id>.json`, `application/json`, the exact bytes of the stored JSON copy (AC-007-02) |

User input appears only in plain text bodies, so line breaks, header-like text and markup stay literal text (AC-006-02); no header is built from user input except the participant address, which V-03 restricts.
