# Test strategy

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: every phase that writes or runs tests · Agent: read-only

When each test level is written and whether it is frozen is defined in `general/phases.md`. Project thresholds are in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md`.

## Constraints

- Do not test acceptance behaviour through internals; use the component's public interface (API, UI, CLI, messages).
- Do not depend on live external services in automated tests; use the local substitutes in `project/00_setup/environments.md` and list the real services in the release notes for manual testing.
- Do not leave flaky, skipped or disabled tests; fix them or record a decision.
- Do not weaken an assertion to make an incorrect implementation pass.
- Test names contain the AC id they verify.

## First complete run

Record the result of the first full run before fixing anything, then classify each failure:

| Class | Action |
|---|---|
| Implementation defect | fix the code |
| Defect in a non-frozen test | fix the test and say so in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` |
| Frozen test appears wrong | blocking decision; do not touch the test |

## Measures (recorded in every project)

Test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`: what each covers, at which level and with which tool.

## Manifest

`docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256` uses `sha256sum` format with paths relative to `02_output/`, hashed after LF normalisation.
# Measurement scope

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 3, 5, 6 · Agent: read-only

Defines what test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size mean, so that figures from different runs compare. Record every figure in `run-log.json` → `codeMetrics` and in `docs/06_verification-report.md` with its scope, level and tool. The project selects paths and exclusions in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Mutation scope"); this file never names them.

## Constraints

- Do not change a tool's scope, filters, exclusions or thresholds to improve a number. A change is a decision record.
- Do not report a figure without its scope, level and tool.
- Production code is the source a component ships. It excludes tests, generated code, the application entry point and anything listed under "Measurement exclusions" in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with a reason. Decide the exclusions in phase 3, before any test is written; do not extend them later.
- Test code never counts towards coverage or mutation.

## Test counts

Per component and level (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e`), passed and failed, from the runner's own report.

## Coverage

Line and branch, per component, as three figures: `unit` (unit tests only), `nonUnit` (integration, acceptance and end-to-end tests that exercise the component) and `all` (one merged report). The headline figure is `all`.

## Mutation score

- **Scope:** all production code of the component, narrowed only to the paths in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` "Mutation scope", which are the same in every run of the project (default: all production code). Do not narrow it by running only some tests or by excluding packages that are not listed there.
- **Tests:** the component's full automated suite, at every level it has, so the score does not depend on which level the agent ran. If that is infeasible, record the tests actually run and the reason in a decision record.
- **Record:** `{score, scoreAdjusted, scoreCovered, killed, equivalent, total, covered, scope, tests, tool, excluded}`. `score` (raw) = killed (timed-out counts as killed) ÷ all mutants the tool generated; a mutant no test reaches counts as survived. `scoreAdjusted` = (killed + equivalent) ÷ total, where `equivalent` is the number of survivors justified as equivalent. `scoreCovered` = killed ÷ mutants a test reaches.
- Do not remove equivalent mutants by hand. List every survivor you count as equivalent in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with the class and method, the mutation and the reason it cannot change behaviour; a survivor without that entry is not equivalent. Always record the raw score next to the adjusted score.

## Code size

`cloc` (same version in every run): production = non-test source and resources, test = test sources including end-to-end tests. Generated code and lock files are excluded.

## Mutation run discipline

- Measure coverage and mutation score in phase 5, so that surviving mutants are handled before verification. Phase 6 repeats a measurement only for a component whose code or tests changed since, and only once, after the last fix.
- Do not start a full mutation run on code that is not final. One full run per component per measurement; the only other runs are the targeted survivor rounds and, only when the rule below requires it, one confirming full run.
- Check once, before the full run, that the tool works: a mutant in code the tests plainly cover must be killed. A score far below the line coverage (for example 25 % at 100 % coverage) means the tool is not activating mutants (known case: Stryker with the wrong Vitest major version); stop and raise a decision, do not record the figure.
- Start a long run in the background and continue with other checks of the phase; read its log only for the summary lines. Do not hold the session in a blocking wait on it.

## Quality gate

The gate is the same in every run of the project: the thresholds in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Thresholds"), per component, over the scope and with the tests defined above. It makes runs comparable: every run reaches the same quality, and what differs is the cost of reaching it.

- **Gate:** line coverage (`all`) at or above the line threshold, and `scoreAdjusted` at or above the mutation threshold. Branch coverage is recorded only.
- **Order in phase 5:** write the unit and integration tests area by area and measure line coverage after each area (fast) until the line threshold is met; then run mutation testing **once** per component (full run); then, if `scoreAdjusted` is below the threshold, up to **three** survivor rounds: each adds tests aimed at the survivors in the code that matters most (validation, security, persistence, business rules first) and re-runs only the mutated classes. After each round recompute `scoreAdjusted` for the component from the last full run plus the re-run classes (the classes that were not re-run keep their killed and total counts from the full run) and write the per-class numbers into `docs/03_test-strategy.md`. If the recomputed score is at least 1.0 point above the threshold the gate is met and no full run follows. Only a recomputed score less than 1.0 point above the threshold, or a change to a class outside the re-run set, needs the one confirming full run; its result then replaces the recomputed one.
- **Stop at the gate:** once a component meets both thresholds, add no further test and start no further mutation run for it. Do not add tests for coverage or score beyond the gate.
- **Shortfall:** after the third round a component still below a threshold is recorded as a shortfall (which threshold, by how many points) in a non-blocking decision and as a finding, and the run continues. Do not change the scope, the tests run or the exclusions to reach a threshold; that is a decision record at most.
- **Record in `run-log.json`:** `codeMetrics.gate` = `{ thresholds: {lineCoverage, mutationScore}, perComponent: { <name>: { lineMet, mutationMet, lineShortfall, mutationShortfall } }, mutationRounds: { <name>: n }, testsAtFirstMutation: { <name>: n }, met: true|false }`; `mutationRounds` is 0 when the first full run already met the gate.

5. Self-check every assertion and helper before the freeze, because a defective frozen test costs a blocking decision: confirm that a correct implementation can make it pass, and that it cannot pass or fail for the wrong reason. A test must not contradict another assertion in the same test.
6. Format and lint the tests now; after freezing they cannot change.
7. Commit the tests story by story as you finish them. Then write the manifest (normalised line endings) and commit it alone as the freeze commit.

# Backend image: build the jar first with ./mvnw package (see README)
FROM eclipse-temurin:21.0.10_7-jre-alpine

RUN addgroup -S app && adduser -S -G app app \
    && mkdir -p /data/json-copies /app \
    && chown -R app:app /data /app

WORKDIR /app
COPY --chown=app:app target/registration-backend-*.jar /app/app.jar

USER app
EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75", "-jar", "/app/app.jar"]

*
!target/registration-backend-*.jar

# Build stage: type check and bundle the single page app
FROM node:24.13.0-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json .npmrc ./
RUN npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
COPY index.html tsconfig.json vite.config.ts ./
COPY src ./src
RUN npx tsc --noEmit && npx vite build

# Runtime: static files served by nginx as the unprivileged nginx user (SB-11)
FROM nginx:1.30.5-alpine
COPY nginx.conf /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
COPY --from=build /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
RUN chown -R nginx:nginx /var/cache/nginx /usr/share/nginx/html
USER nginx
EXPOSE 8080

# Local stack: docker compose --env-file ../.env up --build   (build the backend jar first)
name: registration

services:
  db:
    image: postgres:16.15-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: registration
      POSTGRES_USER: registration
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U registration -d registration"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

  mailpit:
    image: axllent/mailpit:v1.31.1
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8025:8025"
      - "127.0.0.1:1025:1025"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "/mailpit", "readyz"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

  backend:
    build: ./backend
    environment:
      APP_ENVIRONMENT: local
      SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL: jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/registration
      SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME: registration
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
      SMTP_HOST: mailpit
      SMTP_PORT: "1025"
      SMTP_TLS: "false"
      MAIL_FROM: ${MAIL_FROM:-registration@konferenca.si}
      CONFERENCE_NAME: ${CONFERENCE_NAME:-Konferenca 2026}
      CONFERENCE_CONFIG: ${CONFERENCE_CONFIG:-classpath:conference.json}
      JSON_COPY_DIR: /data/json-copies
      CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE: ${CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE:-true}
      RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY: ${RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY:-}
      RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY: ${RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY:-}
      ORGANIZER_USERNAME: ${ORGANIZER_USERNAME:?set ORGANIZER_USERNAME in .env}
      ORGANIZER_PASSWORD: ${ORGANIZER_PASSWORD:?set ORGANIZER_PASSWORD in .env}
      ORGANIZER_EMAILS: ${ORGANIZER_EMAILS:?set ORGANIZER_EMAILS in .env}
      ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY: ${ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY:-false}
      RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE: ${RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE:-60}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"
    volumes:
      - json-copies:/data/json-copies
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
      mailpit:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "-O", "/dev/null", "http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health/readiness"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30
      start_period: 20s

  frontend:
    build: ./frontend
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8081:8080"
    depends_on:
      backend:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "-O", "/dev/null", "http://127.0.0.1:8080/"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

volumes:
  pgdata:
  json-copies:

      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U registration -d registration"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

  mailpit:
    image: axllent/mailpit:v1.31.1
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8025:8025"
      - "127.0.0.1:1025:1025"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "/mailpit", "readyz"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

  backend:
    build: ./backend
    environment:
      APP_ENVIRONMENT: local
      SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL: jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/registration
      SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME: registration
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
      SMTP_HOST: mailpit
      SMTP_PORT: "1025"
      SMTP_TLS: "false"
      MAIL_FROM: ${MAIL_FROM:-registration@konferenca.si}
      CONFERENCE_NAME: ${CONFERENCE_NAME:-Konferenca 2026}
      CONFERENCE_CONFIG: ${CONFERENCE_CONFIG:-classpath:conference.json}
      JSON_COPY_DIR: /data/json-copies
      CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE: ${CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE:-true}
      RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY: ${RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY:-}
      RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY: ${RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY:-}
      ORGANIZER_USERNAME: ${ORGANIZER_USERNAME:?set ORGANIZER_USERNAME in .env}
      ORGANIZER_PASSWORD: ${ORGANIZER_PASSWORD:?set ORGANIZER_PASSWORD in .env}
      ORGANIZER_EMAILS: ${ORGANIZER_EMAILS:?set ORGANIZER_EMAILS in .env}
      ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY: ${ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY:-false}
      RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE: ${RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE:-60}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"
    volumes:
      - json-copies:/data/json-copies
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
      mailpit:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "-O", "/dev/null", "http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health/readiness"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30
      start_period: 20s

  frontend:
    build: ./frontend
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8081:8080"
    depends_on:
      backend:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "-O", "/dev/null", "http://127.0.0.1:8080/"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

I'll fix it by writing compact JSON and sending the attachment base64-encoded so bytes stay untouched.

U="$(sed -n 's/^ORGANIZER_USERNAME=//p' $ENV | tr -d '\r')"
P="$(sed -n 's/^ORGANIZER_PASSWORD=//p' $ENV | tr -d '\r')"
sql() { $DC exec -T db psql -U registration -d registration -tAc "$1"; }
wait_healthy() {
  for i in $(seq 1 60); do
    s=$($DC ps --format '{{.Service}}={{.Health}}' | tr '\n' ' ')
    case "$s" in *backend=healthy*) case "$s" in *frontend=healthy*) echo "$s"; return 0;; esac;; esac
    sleep 3
  done
  echo "NOT HEALTHY: $s"; return 1
}
step() { echo; echo "== $1"; }

step "build and start the stack"
$DC up -d --build >/dev/null 2>&1; wait_healthy

step "health and readiness (NFR-04)"
for p in /actuator/health /actuator/health/liveness /actuator/health/readiness; do
  printf '%s -> ' "$p"; curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8080$p"; echo
done

step "registrations through the frontend proxy (DoD-P01)"
T=$(date +%s)
curl -s -o /tmp/ext.json -w 'external %{http_code}\n' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data "{\"type\":\"EXTERNAL\",\"firstName\":\"Demo\",\"lastName\":\"Zunanji$T\",\"email\":\"ext$T@example.org\",\"organization\":\"Društvo Šentjur\",\"options\":[\"ws-ai\",\"ev-dinner\"],\"consents\":[\"privacy\"],\"captchaToken\":\"test-pass\"}" \
  http://127.0.0.1:8081/api/registrations
curl -s -o /tmp/stu.json -w 'student %{http_code}\n' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data "{\"type\":\"STUDENT\",\"firstName\":\"Demo\",\"lastName\":\"Študent$T\",\"email\":\"stu$T@example.org\",\"studyInstitution\":\"Univerza v Ljubljani\",\"studyProgramme\":\"Računalništvo\",\"studentId\":\"63$T\",\"options\":[\"ev-student-meetup\"],\"consents\":[\"privacy\"],\"captchaToken\":\"test-pass\"}" \
  http://127.0.0.1:8081/api/registrations
EXT=$(sed 's/.*"id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/' /tmp/ext.json); STU=$(sed 's/.*"id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/' /tmp/stu.json)
echo "ids: external $EXT student $STU"

step "stored in PostgreSQL and as JSON copies (DoD-P02)"
sql "select type, last_name, coalesce(organization, study_institution) from registration where id in ('$EXT','$STU') order by type"
$DC exec -T backend ls /data/json-copies | grep -E "$EXT|$STU"

step "emails in Mailpit (DoD-P03)"
for who in "ext$T" "stu$T"; do
  curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8025/api/v1/search?query=$who" | node -e '
    let d="";process.stdin.on("data",c=>d+=c).on("end",()=>{const m=JSON.parse(d).messages;
    console.log(process.argv[1], m.length, "messages:", m.map(x=>x.Subject+" -> "+x.To.map(t=>t.Address).join(",")+" attachments "+x.Attachments).join(" | "))})' "$who"
done

step "export (DoD-P04)"
curl -s -o /tmp/export.xlsx -w 'with credentials %{http_code} %{content_type} %{size_download} bytes\n' -u "$U:$P" http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/export
unzip -l /tmp/export.xlsx 2>/dev/null | grep -E "sheet1.xml|sharedStrings" | awk '{print "  workbook part:", $4}'
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'without credentials %{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/export
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'wrong credentials %{http_code}\n' -u "$U:wrong-password" http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/export

step "search (DoD-P06)"
curl -s -u "$U:$P" "http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/registrations?text=Zunanji$T" | node -e 'let d="";process.stdin.on("data",c=>d+=c).on("end",()=>{const r=JSON.parse(d);console.log("by last name: total",r.total,r.items.map(i=>i.type+" "+i.lastName).join(", "))})'
curl -s -u "$U:$P" "http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/registrations?type=STUDENT" | node -e 'let d="";process.stdin.on("data",c=>d+=c).on("end",()=>{const r=JSON.parse(d);console.log("by type STUDENT: total",r.total,"all students:",r.items.every(i=>i.type==="STUDENT"))})'
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'search without credentials %{http_code}\n' "http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/registrations?text=Zunanji$T"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'organizer page %{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8081/organizer

step "rejections, limits and headers (SR-01, SR-03, SB-10)"
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"type":"EXTERNAL","firstName":"A","lastName":"B","email":"a@b.si","organization":"O","consents":["privacy"],"captchaToken":"wrong"}' http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/registrations
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8081/ | grep -iE "^(content-security-policy|x-frame-options|x-content-type-options|referrer-policy)" | cut -c1-90
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/form-config | grep -iE "^(content-security-policy|x-frame-options|x-content-type-options|referrer-policy|cache-control)"
echo "containers run as: frontend=$($DC exec -T frontend id -un) backend=$($DC exec -T backend id -un)"

COUNT_BEFORE=$(sql "select count(*) from registration"); FILES_BEFORE=$($DC exec -T backend sh -c 'ls /data/json-copies | wc -l' | tr -d ' \r')
step "recreate every container (NFR-02)"
echo "before: $COUNT_BEFORE rows, $FILES_BEFORE JSON copies"
$DC down >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "containers after down: $($DC ps -a -q | wc -l)"
$DC up -d >/dev/null 2>&1; wait_healthy
echo "after: $(sql "select count(*) from registration") rows, $($DC exec -T backend sh -c 'ls /data/json-copies | wc -l' | tr -d ' \r') JSON copies"
sql "select last_name from registration where id = '$EXT'"

step "HTTPS-only organizer access at runtime (SR-06, D-11)"
ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=true $DC up -d backend >/dev/null 2>&1; wait_healthy >/dev/null
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' -u "$U:$P" http://127.0.0.1:8081/api/registrations
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'export over plain HTTP from the host (not loopback inside the container) %{http_code}\n' -u "$U:$P" http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/export
$DC up -d backend >/dev/null 2>&1; wait_healthy >/dev/null
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'export with HTTPS-only off again %{http_code}\n' -u "$U:$P" http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/export

# Conference registration

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-06 · Agent: writes

## Overview

Online registration for a conference: external participants and students register through a public form protected by reCAPTCHA; every accepted registration is stored in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy, confirmed by email to the participant and announced to the organizers with the JSON attached. Organizers sign in to search the registrations and download them as an Excel workbook. Workshops, events, meals and other activities, and the consents, come from a configuration file.

## Components

| Component | What it is | README |
|---|---|---|
| backend | Spring Boot REST API under `/api` (Java 21, PostgreSQL, Flyway, SMTP, Apache POI) | [backend/README.md](backend/README.md) |
| frontend | React single-page app (registration form at `/`, organizer search at `/organizer`), served by nginx, which proxies `/api` to the backend | [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md) |
| local stack | `docker-compose.yml`: PostgreSQL, Mailpit (mail catcher), backend, frontend | this file |

## Quick start (local stack)

Prerequisites: JDK 21, Docker Engine with Compose, Node.js 24 with npm 11 (only for the frontend tools and the end-to-end tests).

1. At the repository root, copy `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` to `.env` and fill `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (at least 16 characters) and `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`. reCAPTCHA keys are not needed locally (test mode).
2. Build the backend jar (the backend image copies it):

   ```sh
   cd 02_output/backend
   ./mvnw -B package -DskipTests
   ```

3. Start the stack from `02_output`:

   ```sh
   cd 02_output
   docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build
   docker compose --env-file ../.env ps        # wait until all four services are healthy
   ```

4. Use it:

   | What | Where |
   |---|---|
   | Registration form | http://127.0.0.1:8081/ (reCAPTCHA test mode) |
   | Organizer search | http://127.0.0.1:8081/organizer (credentials from `.env`) |
   | Excel export | `curl -u <user>:<password> -o registrations.xlsx http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/export` |
   | REST API | http://127.0.0.1:8080/api (contract: `docs/02_contracts/openapi.json`) |
   | Health | http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health/readiness |
   | Emails | Mailpit at http://127.0.0.1:8025 |

5. Stop with `docker compose --env-file ../.env down`; data stays in the volumes `pgdata` and `json-copies` (`down -v` deletes it).

Settings that `docker compose` takes from the environment: `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` (default `true` locally), `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` (default 60), `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` (default `false` locally), plus `CONFERENCE_NAME` and `CONFERENCE_CONFIG`. Example: `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=200 docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d`.

End-to-end tests (Chromium) against the running stack: see [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md#test).

## Documentation

| Document | Content |
|---|---|
| [docs/02_specification.md](docs/02_specification.md) | specification, traceability of AC, SR, SB, NFR, AR |
| [docs/02_contracts/](docs/02_contracts/) | OpenAPI, JSON schemas (JSON copy, conference configuration), database, emails, reCAPTCHA, UI |
| [docs/01_requirements-check.md](docs/01_requirements-check.md) | stories → criteria |
| [docs/03_test-strategy.md](docs/03_test-strategy.md) | test levels, runs, coverage and mutation figures |
| [docs/06_verification-report.md](docs/06_verification-report.md) | definition of done, runtime demonstration, security evidence, findings |
| [docs/release-notes.md](docs/release-notes.md) | delivered scope, limitations, manual tests, pending decisions |
| [docs/decisions-log.md](docs/decisions-log.md) | decision records D-01 … D-16 |
| [docs/00_preflight-report.md](docs/00_preflight-report.md) | environment and dependency checks |

# Backend

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-05, ES-06 · Agent: writes

Spring Boot REST API for the conference registration: form configuration, registrations (stored in PostgreSQL and as JSON copies, then emailed), organizer search and Excel export. Contract: `../docs/02_contracts/openapi.json`. Packages (ports and adapters, checked by ArchUnit): `domain`, `application`, `adapter.{persistence,jsoncopy,mail,captcha,export,web}`, `config`.

## Prerequisites

- JDK 21 (`java -version`); Maven is not needed, the wrapper `./mvnw` downloads Maven 3.9.9.
- Docker Engine for the tests (Testcontainers starts PostgreSQL and Mailpit) and for the container image.
- For running outside Docker: a PostgreSQL 16 database and an SMTP server.

## Configuration

Every setting is an environment variable (ES-01). Secrets (from `.env`, see `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example`) have no default.

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `APP_ENVIRONMENT` | `production` | `local`, `test` or `production`; production refuses unsafe settings at start-up |
| `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL`, `SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME` | none | JDBC URL and user, e.g. `jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/registration` |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | none (secret) | database password |
| `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_TLS` | none, `587`, `true` | mail server; STARTTLS required when `SMTP_TLS=true` |
| `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | empty (secret) | SMTP login, only when the server needs one |
| `MAIL_FROM` | `registration@konferenca.si` | sender address |
| `CONFERENCE_NAME` | `Conference` | name used in the emails |
| `CONFERENCE_CONFIG` | none (required) | options and consents file: `classpath:conference.json` (shipped) or `file:/path/conference.json`; schema `../docs/02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`; the backend refuses to start with an invalid file |
| `JSON_COPY_DIR` | `/data/json-copies` | directory of the raw JSON copies (persistent volume) |
| `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | `false` | `true` accepts only the token `test-pass` and never calls Google; refused in production |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | empty (secret) | reCAPTCHA v2 keys; required in production |
| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | Google siteverify | changed only by tests |
| `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | none (secret) | the organizer login (HTTP Basic); the password is kept only as a BCrypt hash |
| `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | none (secret) | comma-separated notification addresses; each gets its own message |
| `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | `true` | refuse organizer requests over plain HTTP from non-local clients (403); must stay `true` in production |
| `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` | empty | one allowed origin for local development only; refused in production |
| `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | `60` | requests per minute per client and endpoint on `/api` (then 429) |
| `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` | `16384` | request body limit (then 413) |

To change the programme, edit a copy of `src/main/resources/conference.json`, point `CONFERENCE_CONFIG` at it and restart; no code change.

## Build

```sh
./mvnw -B package -DskipTests          # target/registration-backend-0.1.0.jar
```

## Test

```sh
./mvnw -B verify                       # 227 tests: unit, architecture, acceptance (needs Docker); JaCoCo report in target/site/jacoco
./mvnw -B test-compile org.pitest:pitest-maven:mutationCoverage   # mutation testing, report in target/pit-reports (about 25 minutes)
```

## Check

```sh
./mvnw -B spotless:check compile pmd:check pmd:cpd-check spotbugs:check   # format, lint, duplication, static analysis
./mvnw -B dependency-check:check       # dependency scan; export NVD_API_KEY from .env first
```

`./mvnw spotless:apply` formats the code (google-java-format).

## Run

In the local stack: see `../README.md`. Alone (with your own PostgreSQL and SMTP):

```sh
export APP_ENVIRONMENT=local CONFERENCE_CONFIG=classpath:conference.json CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true \
       SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://127.0.0.1:5432/registration SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME=registration \
```

The external nginx terminates TLS, serves `/` from the frontend container and forwards `/api` to the backend. It must set the upstream `Host` itself and pass the client address and scheme, so that rate limiting and the HTTPS-only check see the real client:

```nginx

    proxy_pass http://backend:8080;
    proxy_set_header Host backend;                 # never forward the client's Host
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr; # replaces any client-sent value
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;    # https
    client_max_body_size 32k;
}
```

The backend trusts `X-Forwarded-*` only from loopback or private addresses, so it must not be reachable from the internet except through this proxy.

|---|---|
| Start-up fails with `Invalid configuration: …` | a required or unsafe setting; the message names it (never its value) |
| Start-up fails with an `InvalidConfigurationException` | the options file breaks the schema (duplicate id, unknown category, missing name, …) |

| Tests fail at start with Docker errors | Docker is not running; the acceptance tests need it |

| `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | empty (secret) | SMTP login, only when the server needs one |
| `MAIL_FROM` | `registration@konferenca.si` | sender address |
| `CONFERENCE_NAME` | `Conference` | name used in the emails |

# Frontend

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-05, ES-06 · Agent: writes

React single-page app: the registration form at `/` (type choice, the type's fields, options grouped by category, consents, reCAPTCHA, confirmation) and the organizer search page at `/organizer` (sign-in, search, type and option filters, paging). It talks only to `/api` on its own origin (AR-01); in the container, nginx serves the static files and proxies `/api` to the backend. UI contract: `../docs/02_contracts/ui.md`.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 24.13.0 with npm 11.6.2 (`.npmrc` enforces the engines and exact versions).
- For the end-to-end tests: the running local stack (`../README.md`) and Playwright's Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium` once, if not yet installed).

## Configuration

The frontend has no secret and no build-time setting (AR-07). The reCAPTCHA site key and test mode come from `GET /api/form-config` at runtime. The nginx configuration is `nginx.conf` (port 8080, user `nginx`, security headers, `/api` proxy to `backend:8080`).

## Build

```sh
npm ci
npm run build          # type check and bundle into dist/
```

## Test

```sh
npm test               # 62 tests: unit (src/**/*.test.*) and acceptance (tests/acceptance)
npm run test:coverage  # with V8 coverage in coverage/
npm run mutation       # Stryker mutation testing, report in reports/mutation (about 25 minutes)
```

End-to-end tests (6 scenarios, `tests/e2e`) against the running local stack, with the organizer credentials from `.env`:

```sh
export ORGANIZER_USERNAME="$(sed -n 's/^ORGANIZER_USERNAME=//p' ../../.env | tr -d '\r')"
export ORGANIZER_PASSWORD="$(sed -n 's/^ORGANIZER_PASSWORD=//p' ../../.env | tr -d '\r')"
npm run test:e2e
```

They use `http://127.0.0.1:8081` (frontend), `http://127.0.0.1:8080` (backend), `http://127.0.0.1:8025` (Mailpit) and `docker compose exec` on the services `db` and `backend`; override with `E2E_BASE_URL`, `E2E_BACKEND_URL`, `E2E_MAILPIT_URL`, `E2E_COMPOSE_FILE`, `E2E_ENV_FILE`. The stack must run with `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true` (the local default).

## Check

```sh
npm run check          # Prettier, ESLint, tsc --noEmit
npm run duplication    # jscpd
npm audit --omit=dev   # dependency scan of the shipped packages
```

`npm run format` formats the sources.

## Run

- Development server with hot reload, proxying `/api` to a backend on `127.0.0.1:8080`: `npm run dev` (http://127.0.0.1:5173).
- Production-like: the `frontend` service of `../docker-compose.yml` (http://127.0.0.1:8081), built by `Dockerfile` (Node build stage, nginx runtime).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and remedy |
|---|---|
| "The registration form could not be loaded" | the backend is not reachable on `/api` (dev server: start the backend on 8080) |
| `npm ci` fails with an engine error | Node or npm differ from 24.13.0 / 11.6.2 |
| e2e tests fail with `Set ORGANIZER_USERNAME and ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | export them from `.env` as shown above |
| e2e tests fail at the first page | the stack is not running or not healthy (`docker compose ps`) |
| No reCAPTCHA widget, "reCAPTCHA test mode" shown | the backend runs with `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true` |

# Release notes

> Written in: phase 7 · Agent: writes

Version 0.1.0, 2026-10-22.

## Delivered

| Story | Delivered |
|---|---|
| US-001, US-002 | registration forms for external participants and students with backend validation (required fields, email format, active and available options, mandatory consents, reCAPTCHA) |
| US-003 | options and consents from a configuration file (`CONFERENCE_CONFIG`), validated at start-up |
| US-004 | confirmation in the page; field errors next to the fields; general error without details |
| US-005 | storage in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy in one unit of work (no 201 unless both exist) |
| US-006, US-007 | participant confirmation and one organizer notification per address with the JSON copy attached, sent after storage; a mail failure keeps the registration |
| US-008 | Excel export for the organizer (HTTP Basic) |
| US-009 | organizer search page and API: text search, type and option filters, 20 per page, newest first |
| security and operations | rate and size limits, HTTPS-only organizer access, security headers, non-root containers, health and readiness, local compose stack |

All 48 acceptance criteria and 6 end-to-end scenarios pass; quality gate met (backend line 98.32 %, mutation 91.20 %; frontend line 100 %, mutation 93.81 %). Evidence: `docs/06_verification-report.md`.

## Known limitations

- The rate limit is kept in memory per backend instance; several instances behind one proxy each allow the limit.
- There is one organizer account; credentials are entered on the organizer page and kept only in the page's memory (a reload signs out).
- The organizer search page is the only organizer page; there is no administration UI, editing, deletion or filtered export (out of scope).
- The backend image copies a jar built on the host (`./mvnw package` first); the stack is not built from source inside Docker for the backend.
- A configuration change (programme, consents) needs a backend restart.
- Accepted findings: npm `min-release-age` is not set because the pinned npm 11.6.2 does not support it (F-01); Moderate advisories remain in dev-only test tooling (F-07, F-08). See `docs/06_verification-report.md`.
- Registrations and JSON copies are never deleted automatically (OQ-06): **the operator must delete the database rows and the JSON copies no later than 12 months after the conference** (`DELETE FROM registration;` cascades to options and consents; remove the files in the `json-copies` volume).

## Must be tested manually by a human

| # | What | How | Why not automated |
|---|---|---|---|
| M-01 | reCAPTCHA with production keys | set `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`, `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=false`; submit one real registration; then submit with the widget unsolved (expect the captcha error) | tests use test mode and a mocked verification endpoint; no calls to Google |
| M-02 | email delivery to real mailboxes | configure the external SMTP account (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_TLS=true`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`); register; check the participant mailbox and every `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` mailbox, incl. the JSON attachment and č, š, ž | tests use Mailpit |
| M-03 | HTTPS, redirects and `/api` routing on the external nginx | `https://` serves the page, `http://` redirects to HTTPS, `/api/form-config` reaches the backend, the certificate (Let's Encrypt) is valid | no TLS or reverse proxy locally |
| M-04 | proxy headers (SR-08) and HTTPS-only access (SR-06) in production | send a request with a forged `Host` header and check the backend sees the upstream host; sign in on `/organizer` over HTTPS (works) and request `/api/export` over plain HTTP with valid credentials (403, or redirected by the proxy) | needs the production proxy |
| M-05 | production start-up guards | start the backend with `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production` and in turn `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`, empty reCAPTCHA keys, `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false`: it must refuse to start each time | unit-tested only |
| M-06 | data retention | after the conference, delete rows and JSON copies within 12 months (see Known limitations) | an operator procedure |
| M-07 | export opened in Excel | open the downloaded `registrations.xlsx` in Microsoft Excel or LibreOffice; check Slovenian characters and that no cell is evaluated as a formula | tests parse the file programmatically |

## Decisions pending review

| Decision | Applied option | Open question for the reviewer |
|---|---|---|
| D-11 | organizer requests over plain HTTP from a non-local client are answered 403 (field `protocol`) before credentials are checked | is 403 acceptable, or should it be 401 like wrong credentials? The frozen tests accept any 4xx without data |

All other decisions (D-01 … D-16) are resolved; see `docs/decisions-log.md`.

## Readme check from a clean checkout

See the section below, added after the check.

# Conference registration

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-06 · Agent: writes

## Overview

Online registration for a conference: external participants and students register through a public form protected by reCAPTCHA; every accepted registration is stored in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy, confirmed by email to the participant and announced to the organizers with the JSON attached. Organizers sign in to search the registrations and download them as an Excel workbook. Workshops, events, meals and other activities, and the consents, come from a configuration file.

## Components

| Component | What it is | README |
|---|---|---|
| backend | Spring Boot REST API under `/api` (Java 21, PostgreSQL, Flyway, SMTP, Apache POI) | [backend/README.md](backend/README.md) |
| frontend | React single-page app (registration form at `/`, organizer search at `/organizer`), served by nginx, which proxies `/api` to the backend | [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md) |
| local stack | `docker-compose.yml`: PostgreSQL, Mailpit (mail catcher), backend, frontend | this file |

## Quick start (local stack)

Prerequisites: JDK 21, Docker Engine with Compose, Node.js 24 with npm 11 (only for the frontend tools and the end-to-end tests).

1. At the repository root, copy `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` to `.env` and fill `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (at least 16 characters) and `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`. reCAPTCHA keys are not needed locally (test mode).
2. Build the backend jar (the backend image copies it):

   ```sh
   cd 02_output/backend
   ./mvnw -B package -DskipTests
   ```

3. Start the stack from `02_output`:

   ```sh
   cd 02_output
   docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build
   docker compose --env-file ../.env ps        # wait until all four services are healthy
   ```

4. Use it:

   | What | Where |

# Backend

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-05, ES-06 · Agent: writes

Spring Boot REST API for the conference registration: form configuration, registrations (stored in PostgreSQL and as JSON copies, then emailed), organizer search and Excel export. Contract: `../docs/02_contracts/openapi.json`. Packages (ports and adapters, checked by ArchUnit): `domain`, `application`, `adapter.{persistence,jsoncopy,mail,captcha,export,web}`, `config`.

## Prerequisites

- JDK 21 (`java -version`); Maven is not needed, the wrapper `./mvnw` downloads Maven 3.9.9.
- Docker Engine for the tests (Testcontainers starts PostgreSQL and Mailpit) and for the container image.
- For running outside Docker: a PostgreSQL 16 database and an SMTP server.

## Configuration

Every setting is an environment variable (ES-01). Secrets (from `.env`, see `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example`) have no default.

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `APP_ENVIRONMENT` | `production` | `local`, `test` or `production`; production refuses unsafe settings at start-up |
| `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL`, `SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME` | none | JDBC URL and user, e.g. `jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/registration` |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | none (secret) | database password |
| `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_TLS` | none, `587`, `true` | mail server; STARTTLS required when `SMTP_TLS=true` |
| `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | empty (secret) | SMTP login, only when the server needs one |
| `MAIL_FROM` | `registration@konferenca.si` | sender address |
| `CONFERENCE_NAME` | `Conference` | name used in the emails |
| `CONFERENCE_CONFIG` | none (required) | options and consents file: `classpath:conference.json` (shipped) or `file:/path/conference.json`; schema `../docs/02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`; the backend refuses to start with an invalid file |
| `JSON_COPY_DIR` | `/data/json-copies` | directory of the raw JSON copies (persistent volume) |
| `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | `false` | `true` accepts only the token `test-pass` and never calls Google; refused in production |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | empty (secret) | reCAPTCHA v2 keys; required in production |
| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | Google siteverify | changed only by tests |
| `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | none (secret) | the organizer login (HTTP Basic); the password is kept only as a BCrypt hash |
| `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | none (secret) | comma-separated notification addresses; each gets its own message |
| `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | `true` | refuse organizer requests over plain HTTP from non-local clients (403); must stay `true` in production |
| `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` | empty | one allowed origin for local development only; refused in production |
| `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | `60` | requests per minute per client and endpoint on `/api` (then 429) |
| `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` | `16384` | request body limit (then 413) |

To change the programme, edit a copy of `src/main/resources/conference.json`, point `CONFERENCE_CONFIG` at it and restart; no code change.

## Build

```sh
./mvnw -B package -DskipTests          # target/registration-backend-0.1.0.jar
```

## Test

```sh
./mvnw -B verify                       # 227 tests: unit, architecture, acceptance (needs Docker); JaCoCo report in target/site/jacoco
./mvnw -B test-compile org.pitest:pitest-maven:mutationCoverage   # mutation testing, report in target/pit-reports (about 25 minutes)
```

## Check

```sh
./mvnw -B spotless:check compile pmd:check pmd:cpd-check spotbugs:check   # format, lint, duplication, static analysis
./mvnw -B dependency-check:check       # dependency scan; export NVD_API_KEY from .env first
```

`./mvnw spotless:apply` formats the code (google-java-format).

## Run

In the local stack: see `../README.md`. Alone (with your own PostgreSQL and SMTP):

```sh
export APP_ENVIRONMENT=local CONFERENCE_CONFIG=classpath:conference.json CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true \
       SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://127.0.0.1:5432/registration SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME=registration \
       SMTP_HOST=127.0.0.1 SMTP_PORT=1025 SMTP_TLS=false JSON_COPY_DIR=./data/json-copies
# POSTGRES_PASSWORD, ORGANIZER_USERNAME, ORGANIZER_PASSWORD, ORGANIZER_EMAILS from .env
java -jar target/registration-backend-0.1.0.jar
```

The API listens on port 8080; health at `/actuator/health`, `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness` (database and JSON copy directory). The container image (`Dockerfile`) runs as user `app` and expects the jar in `target/`.

## Production behind nginx (SR-04, SR-06, SR-08)

The external nginx terminates TLS, serves `/` from the frontend container and forwards `/api` to the backend. It must set the upstream `Host` itself and pass the client address and scheme, so that rate limiting and the HTTPS-only check see the real client:

```nginx
location /api/ {
    proxy_pass http://backend:8080;
    proxy_set_header Host backend;                 # never forward the client's Host
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr; # replaces any client-sent value
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;    # https
    client_max_body_size 32k;
}
```

The backend trusts `X-Forwarded-*` only from loopback or private addresses, so it must not be reachable from the internet except through this proxy.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and remedy |
|---|---|
| Start-up fails with `Invalid configuration: …` | a required or unsafe setting; the message names it (never its value) |
| Start-up fails with an `InvalidConfigurationException` | the options file breaks the schema (duplicate id, unknown category, missing name, …) |
| Readiness `DOWN` | database unreachable or `JSON_COPY_DIR` not writable |
| Registrations answer 500 | the JSON copy could not be written; nothing was stored (AR-05) |
| Organizer requests answer 403 `protocol` | `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=true` and the request came over plain HTTP from a non-local client |
| 429 | the rate limit; raise `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` for load tests |
| Tests fail at start with Docker errors | Docker is not running; the acceptance tests need it |

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-05, ES-06 · Agent: writes

React single-page app: the registration form at `/` (type choice, the type's fields, options grouped by category, consents, reCAPTCHA, confirmation) and the organizer search page at `/organizer` (sign-in, search, type and option filters, paging). It talks only to `/api` on its own origin (AR-01); in the container, nginx serves the static files and proxies `/api` to the backend. UI contract: `../docs/02_contracts/ui.md`.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 24.13.0 with npm 11.6.2 (`.npmrc` enforces the engines and exact versions).
- For the end-to-end tests: the running local stack (`../README.md`) and Playwright's Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium` once, if not yet installed).

## Configuration

The frontend has no secret and no build-time setting (AR-07). The reCAPTCHA site key and test mode come from `GET /api/form-config` at runtime. The nginx configuration is `nginx.conf` (port 8080, user `nginx`, security headers, `/api` proxy to `backend:8080`).

## Build

```sh
npm ci
npm run build          # type check and bundle into dist/
```

## Test

```sh
npm test               # 62 tests: unit (src/**/*.test.*) and acceptance (tests/acceptance)
npm run test:coverage  # with V8 coverage in coverage/
npm run mutation       # Stryker mutation testing, report in reports/mutation (about 25 minutes)
```

End-to-end tests (6 scenarios, `tests/e2e`) against the running local stack, with the organizer credentials from `.env`:

```sh
export ORGANIZER_USERNAME="$(sed -n 's/^ORGANIZER_USERNAME=//p' ../../.env | tr -d '\r')"
export ORGANIZER_PASSWORD="$(sed -n 's/^ORGANIZER_PASSWORD=//p' ../../.env | tr -d '\r')"
npm run test:e2e
```

They use `http://127.0.0.1:8081` (frontend), `http://127.0.0.1:8080` (backend), `http://127.0.0.1:8025` (Mailpit) and `docker compose exec` on the services `db` and `backend`; override with `E2E_BASE_URL`, `E2E_BACKEND_URL`, `E2E_MAILPIT_URL`, `E2E_COMPOSE_FILE`, `E2E_ENV_FILE`. The stack must run with `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true` (the local default).

## Check

```sh
npm run check          # Prettier, ESLint, tsc --noEmit
npm run duplication    # jscpd
npm audit --omit=dev   # dependency scan of the shipped packages
```

`npm run format` formats the sources.

## Run

- Development server with hot reload, proxying `/api` to a backend on `127.0.0.1:8080`: `npm run dev` (http://127.0.0.1:5173).
- Production-like: the `frontend` service of `../docker-compose.yml` (http://127.0.0.1:8081), built by `Dockerfile` (Node build stage, nginx runtime).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and remedy |
|---|---|
| "The registration form could not be loaded" | the backend is not reachable on `/api` (dev server: start the backend on 8080) |
| `npm ci` fails with an engine error | Node or npm differ from 24.13.0 / 11.6.2 |
| e2e tests fail with `Set ORGANIZER_USERNAME and ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | export them from `.env` as shown above |
| e2e tests fail at the first page | the stack is not running or not healthy (`docker compose ps`) |
| No reCAPTCHA widget, "reCAPTCHA test mode" shown | the backend runs with `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true` |

All 48 acceptance criteria and 6 end-to-end scenarios pass; quality gate met (backend line 98.32 %, mutation 91.20 %; frontend line 100 %, mutation 93.81 %). Evidence: `docs/06_verification-report.md`.

## Known limitations

- The rate limit is kept in memory per backend instance; several instances behind one proxy each allow the limit.

 - Primary working directory: C:\Users\tanej\Documents\LAB\tanej_single-agent_sdd_v001_run-1-search\02_output (was C:\Users\tanej\Documents\LAB\tanej_single-agent_sdd_v001_run-1-search)

<total_tokens>14267733 tokens left</total_tokens>

The run is complete: all eight phases passed and every gate is met. The only open item is D-11, which waits for your review but blocks nothing.

**What was built** (in `02_output/`): a Spring Boot backend and a React frontend for conference registration, plus a local Docker Compose stack (database, mail catcher, backend, frontend). It covers all 9 user stories, the search feature included.

**Results**
- **Tests:** all 295 pass: 227 backend, 62 frontend and 6 end-to-end tests in the browser. The 116 tests frozen before the build were never changed.
- **Quality gate:**

  | Component | Line coverage | Mutation score | Survivor rounds |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Backend | 98.32 % | 91.20 % | 0 |
  | Frontend | 100 % | 93.81 % | 1 |

- **Security scans:** no Critical or High finding. Three Medium findings are accepted with reasons (dev-only npm advisories, and an npm setting that the pinned npm 11.6.2 doesn't support). No `.env` value appears in any file or commit message.
- **Running stack:** both registration types, storage, emails, export and search work. Data survives recreating every container, and organizer access over plain HTTP is refused. Following the READMEs from a fresh clone also works.

**Needs your attention**
- **D-11 (pending review):** organizer requests over plain HTTP from a non-local client get **403**, checked before the credentials. The alternative is 401, like wrong credentials. The frozen tests accept either.
- **Manual tests:** `docs/release-notes.md` lists M-01 … M-07: real reCAPTCHA keys, real mail delivery, HTTPS and proxy routing, production start-up checks, data deletion within 12 months, and opening the export in Excel.

**Where I broke the rules** (all recorded in the run log):
- Two test-harness commits exceed the 400-line limit (849 and 468 lines).
- One commit (`de69bfc`) didn't compile; the next commit fixed it.
- I ran one unnecessary extra frontend mutation run because I misread a surviving mutant. D-15 records the mistake and D-16 corrects it; the first run still counts as the measurement.
- A commit guard caught the size and build problems for the rest of the run.

**About the machine:** your laptop went to sleep three times during long silent tool runs, for about 2¾ hours in total. That only stretched wall time. The post-run report excludes idle gaps, and I didn't change any power settings.

`03_statistics/run-log.json` and `run-summary.md` are left uncommitted for the post-run session. The final agent commit is `bdef67e`, and the stack is stopped.
